ing_salt.whatItIs: Common table salt, a refined mineral that supplies sodium and chloride — two of the electrolytes animals need to regulate fluid balance.
ing_salt.whyItsHere: Added both as an essential mineral and because it makes food taste better to the animal.
ing_salt.whatToWatchFor: An essential mineral, but excess can be harmful, so it is rated safe in moderation rather than simply safe.

ing_choline.whatItIs: A nutrient related to the B vitamins, made synthetically for use in pet food. It plays a part in liver function and in how nerves signal.
ing_choline.whyItsHere: Included as an added nutrient to support liver function and nerve signalling.

ing_chicken.whatItIs: Poultry meat, used here as the main protein in the recipe. It is a whole, minimally processed ingredient rather than a rendered or refined one.
ing_chicken.whyItsHere: Included as the primary protein source, supplying the amino acids the diet is built around.
ing_chicken.whatToWatchFor: Chicken is one of the more common food sensitivities: our data puts the allergen risk at medium for dogs and high for cats.

ing_taurine.whatItIs: An essential amino acid, added in synthetic form. Cats in particular cannot make enough of it themselves and must get it from their diet.
ing_taurine.whyItsHere: Added to make sure the finished food supplies enough taurine, which our data flags as critical for cats.

ing_potassium.whatItIs: An essential mineral supplied in added form. It is one of the electrolytes involved in keeping fluid balance steady.
ing_potassium.whyItsHere: Included as an added nutrient to help the diet meet its electrolyte requirements.

ing_natural_flavor.whatItIs: A flavouring derived from natural sources, usually animal-based. The label term does not say which animal it came from.
ing_natural_flavor.whyItsHere: Added to make the food more appealing to eat — its only job is palatability.
ing_natural_flavor.whatToWatchFor: Because the source animal is not named, our data puts its allergen risk at medium and notes that the risk depends on what it was made from.

ing_vitamin_e.whatItIs: A fat-soluble vitamin derived from natural sources. It acts as an antioxidant, which is also why it is often used to keep fats from going rancid.
ing_vitamin_e.whyItsHere: Included as an essential nutrient and for its antioxidant role in the food.

ing_calcium.whatItIs: An essential mineral supplied in added form, best known for its part in building and maintaining bone and teeth.
ing_calcium.whyItsHere: Added so the finished diet meets its calcium requirement.
ing_calcium.whatToWatchFor: Note: That calcium needs to be balanced against phosphorus rather than simply maximised.

ing_vitamin_b6.whatItIs: An essential B vitamin, added synthetically. Note: It is commonly supplied as pyridoxine hydrochloride under AAFCO conventions.
ing_vitamin_b6.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in amino acid metabolism and nervous system function.

ing_vitamin_b2.whatItIs: An essential B vitamin, added synthetically. It is water-soluble, and our data notes that any excess is excreted rather than stored.
ing_vitamin_b2.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in energy metabolism and general cellular function.

ing_vitamin_b1.whatItIs: Thiamine, an essential B vitamin added in synthetic form. It is involved in nerve function and in how the body releases energy from food.
ing_vitamin_b1.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient in the vitamin premix.
ing_vitamin_b1.whatToWatchFor: Our data flags thiamine as critical for cats, noting that a deficiency causes neurological problems.

ing_folic_acid.whatItIs: An essential B vitamin, added in synthetic form. It takes part in cell division and in building DNA.
ing_folic_acid.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient in the vitamin premix.

ing_vitamin_b5.whatItIs: An essential B vitamin, added synthetically. Note: It is commonly supplied as d-calcium pantothenate under AAFCO conventions.
ing_vitamin_b5.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, used in coenzyme A synthesis and energy metabolism.

ing_iodine.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, supplied in added form. The thyroid gland depends on it to make its hormones.
ing_iodine.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its iodine requirement.
ing_iodine.whatToWatchFor: Note: Iodine is worth monitoring in cats with hyperthyroidism.

ing_rosemary_extract.whatItIs: An extract of the rosemary herb, used at small levels. It has antioxidant properties, which is what makes it useful as a preservative.
ing_rosemary_extract.whyItsHere: Added as a natural antioxidant preservative, to slow fats in the food from going rancid.

ing_vitamin_b12_supplement.whatItIs: A synthesised form of vitamin B12, added to the vitamin premix. Producing it involves considerable processing, which is why it is classed as ultra-processed.
ing_vitamin_b12_supplement.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in red blood cell formation and nerve function.

ing_vitamin_a.whatItIs: A fat-soluble vitamin, supplied here in added form. It is involved in vision and immune function.
ing_vitamin_a.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient in the vitamin premix.
ing_vitamin_a.whatToWatchFor: Our data describes vitamin A as an essential nutrient that is toxic in excess — being fat-soluble, it accumulates rather than being flushed out.

ing_vitamin_d3_supplement.whatItIs: A synthesised form of vitamin D, added to the vitamin premix. It governs how well calcium is absorbed and used for bone.
ing_vitamin_d3_supplement.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, so the diet supports calcium absorption and bone health.
ing_vitamin_d3_supplement.whatToWatchFor: Note: Vitamin D3 is fat-soluble and that excess is toxic, so it accumulates rather than being excreted.

ing_liver.whatItIs: Organ meat, used whole and minimally processed. It is dense in micronutrients and animals generally find it very palatable.
ing_liver.whyItsHere: Included both as a concentrated source of micronutrients and to make the food more appealing.
ing_liver.whatToWatchFor: Note: That excessive intake may contribute to vitamin A excess, and puts liver's allergen risk at medium.

ing_flaxseed.whatItIs: The seed of the flax plant, used whole or ground. It supplies fibre and the plant-form omega-3 that the body can convert.
ing_flaxseed.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and as an omega-3 precursor.

ing_biotin.whatItIs: A B vitamin added in synthetic form, associated with the condition of skin and coat.
ing_biotin.whyItsHere: Included as an added nutrient supporting coat and skin health.

ing_chicken_fat.whatItIs: Fat rendered from chicken. It is an energy-dense ingredient and carries much of a food's aroma and flavour.
ing_chicken_fat.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated energy source and to make the food more palatable.

ing_guar_gum.whatItIs: A soluble fibre extracted from the guar bean. In water it swells into a gel, which is what gives it its thickening effect.
ing_guar_gum.whyItsHere: Added to thicken the food and hold its texture together, particularly in wet formats.

ing_peas.whatItIs: The seed of the pea plant, used whole or split. It contributes both fibre and plant protein.
ing_peas.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and as plant protein alongside the animal protein.

ing_carrots.whatItIs: A root vegetable, used minimally processed. It supplies fibre and beta carotene, the orange pigment the body can turn into vitamin A.
ing_carrots.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and beta carotene.

ing_selenium.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, supplied here as sodium selenite. It works as an antioxidant and the thyroid depends on it.
ing_selenium.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts so the diet meets its selenium requirement.

ing_dl_methionine.whatItIs: An amino acid added in synthetic form. It has an acidifying effect, which is what links it to urinary pH.
ing_dl_methionine.whyItsHere: Added to help keep urinary pH in the intended range. This entry applies to cat foods.

ing_mixed_tocopherols.whatItIs: A group of vitamin E compounds extracted from vegetable oils. They are antioxidants, which is what makes them useful for preserving fats.
ing_mixed_tocopherols.whyItsHere: Added as a natural preservative to slow the fats in the food from going rancid. Our data calls it the preferred natural preservative.

ing_brown_rice.whatItIs: Whole-grain rice with the bran layer left on, so it keeps more fibre than white rice.
ing_brown_rice.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source, and it helps bind kibble together.

ing_salmon.whatItIs: An oily fish, used as a protein source. Its fat is naturally rich in omega-3.
ing_salmon.whyItsHere: Included both for its protein and as a source of omega-3 fats.
ing_salmon.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts salmon's allergen risk at low for dogs but high for cats.

ing_sweet_potatoes.whatItIs: A starchy root vegetable, used minimally processed. It supplies both fibre and carbohydrate.
ing_sweet_potatoes.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and for its fibre.

ing_iron.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, supplied here as ferrous sulfate. Red blood cells need it to carry oxygen.
ing_iron.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its iron requirement.

ing_copper.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, supplied as copper sulfate. It is involved in enzyme function and in coat pigment.
ing_copper.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts so the diet meets its copper requirement.
ing_copper.whatToWatchFor: Note: That some breeds, such as Bedlington Terriers, are sensitive to copper.

ing_fish_oil.whatItIs: Oil pressed from fish. It is one of the richest sources of the long-chain omega-3 fats.
ing_fish_oil.whyItsHere: Added as an omega-3 source, associated in our data with an anti-inflammatory role.

ing_cranberries.whatItIs: A tart berry, used whole or dried. It is associated with urinary tract health.

ing_zinc.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, supplied as zinc sulfate. It is involved in immune function and skin health.
ing_zinc.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its zinc requirement.
ing_zinc.whatToWatchFor: Note: That Huskies and Malamutes may need more zinc than other dogs.

ing_sunflower_oil.whatItIs: Oil pressed from sunflower seeds. It is a source of omega-6 fats.
ing_sunflower_oil.whyItsHere: Added as a fat source, associated in our data with coat health.

ing_turkey.whatItIs: Poultry meat used as the main protein in the recipe, whole and minimally processed.
ing_turkey.whyItsHere: Included as the primary protein source for the diet.
ing_turkey.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts turkey's allergen risk at medium — poultry is a reasonably common food sensitivity.

ing_chicken_meal.whatItIs: Chicken that has been rendered and dried, so most of the water and fat is removed. That leaves a much more concentrated protein than fresh chicken.
ing_chicken_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source; by weight it delivers more protein than fresh meat does.
ing_chicken_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts the allergen risk at medium for dogs and high for cats, the same sensitivity that applies to chicken generally.

ing_tricalcium_phosphate.whatItIs: A synthesised mineral compound supplying both calcium and phosphorus.
ing_tricalcium_phosphate.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its calcium and phosphorus requirements.

ing_niacin.whatItIs: Vitamin B3, added in synthetic form. It takes part in metabolism and is associated with skin health.
ing_niacin.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient in the vitamin premix.

ing_pumpkin.whatItIs: A squash, used minimally processed. It is a well-known source of soluble fibre.
ing_pumpkin.whyItsHere: Included as a source of soluble fibre.

ing_beef.whatItIs: Meat from cattle, used as the main protein in the recipe.
ing_beef.whyItsHere: Included as the primary protein source for the diet.
ing_beef.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts beef's allergen risk at medium for dogs and high for cats; beef is among the more commonly reported food sensitivities.

ing_manganese.whatItIs: An essential trace mineral, added in synthetic form. It is involved in bone development and in metabolism.
ing_manganese.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its manganese requirement.

ing_blueberries.whatItIs: A small berry, used whole or dried, included for its antioxidant content.
ing_blueberries.whyItsHere: Included as a source of antioxidants.

ing_glycerin.whatItIs: A syrupy liquid derived from fats and oils. It holds on to water, which keeps softer foods from drying out.
ing_glycerin.whyItsHere: Added to retain moisture, so semi-moist foods and treats stay soft.

ing_copper_proteinate.whatItIs: Copper bound to amino acids rather than supplied as a plain salt. Our data describes this chelated form as more bioavailable.
ing_copper_proteinate.whyItsHere: Added as a more absorbable copper source, associated with connective tissue health.

ing_manganese_proteinate.whatItIs: Manganese bound to amino acids rather than supplied as a plain salt. Our data describes this chelated form as more bioavailable.
ing_manganese_proteinate.whyItsHere: Added as a more absorbable manganese source, associated with bone development.

ing_zinc_proteinate.whatItIs: Zinc bound to amino acids rather than supplied as a plain salt. Our data describes this chelated form as more bioavailable.
ing_zinc_proteinate.whyItsHere: Added as a more absorbable zinc source, associated with skin and coat health.

ing_citric_acid.whatItIs: An acid found naturally in citrus fruit and produced commercially for food use.
ing_citric_acid.whyItsHere: Added as a preservative and to enhance flavour.

ing_tapioca_starch.whatItIs: Starch extracted from the cassava root. Our data describes it as a grain-free starch alternative that is easily digestible.
ing_tapioca_starch.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and to thicken or bind the food.

ing_dried_egg_product.whatItIs: Dehydrated egg. Our data describes it as a complete protein and notes it may include shell fragments under AAFCO conventions.
ing_dried_egg_product.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and as a binder holding the food together.
ing_dried_egg_product.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and notes the product may include shell fragments.

ing_xanthan_gum.whatItIs: A thickener produced by fermenting sugars with a bacterium. Very small amounts thicken a lot of liquid.
ing_xanthan_gum.whyItsHere: Added to thicken the food and keep its texture stable.

ing_water.whatItIs: Water, listed because wet and semi-moist foods are largely made of it.
ing_water.whyItsHere: Present as the base the rest of the recipe is mixed into.

ing_salmon_oil.whatItIs: Oil from salmon, one of the richest sources of long-chain omega-3 fats.
ing_salmon_oil.whyItsHere: Added as an omega-3 source, associated in our data with an anti-inflammatory role.

ing_l_carnitine.whatItIs: A compound made from amino acids, added in synthetic form. It helps move fat into cells to be burned for energy.
ing_l_carnitine.whyItsHere: Added for its role in fat metabolism and, per our data, its association with heart health.

ing_dried_chicory_root.whatItIs: The dried root of the chicory plant. It is a well-known source of prebiotic fibre — fibre that feeds gut bacteria rather than the animal.
ing_dried_chicory_root.whyItsHere: Included as a prebiotic fibre supporting the gut's own bacteria.

ing_potatoes.whatItIs: A starchy tuber, used cooked. It supplies carbohydrate and helps hold kibble together.
ing_potatoes.whyItsHere: Included as a starch source and as a binder.

ing_dicalcium_phosphate.whatItIs: A synthesised mineral supplying calcium and phosphorus, and the form most often used in pet food.
ing_dicalcium_phosphate.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its calcium and phosphorus requirements.

ing_oats.whatItIs: A whole cereal grain, minimally processed. It supplies both carbohydrate and fibre.
ing_oats.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and for its fibre.

ing_iron_proteinate.whatItIs: Iron bound to amino acids rather than supplied as a plain salt. Our data describes this chelated form as more bioavailable.
ing_iron_proteinate.whyItsHere: Added as a more absorbable iron source, supporting oxygen transport in the blood.

ing_barley.whatItIs: A cereal grain, minimally processed, supplying carbohydrate and fibre.
ing_barley.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and for its fibre.

ing_kelp.whatItIs: A seaweed, used dried. It carries a range of minerals and is a notably concentrated natural source of iodine.
ing_kelp.whyItsHere: Included as a mineral source, particularly for iodine.
ing_kelp.whatToWatchFor: Because kelp is concentrated in iodine, rated safe in moderation and says to monitor iodine intake.

ing_spinach.whatItIs: A leafy green, used minimally processed. It carries iron and a range of vitamins.
ing_spinach.whyItsHere: Included as a source of iron and vitamins.
ing_spinach.whatToWatchFor: Note: Spinach is high in oxalates and should be avoided for pets with kidney issues, and rates it safe in moderation.

ing_tuna.whatItIs: An oily marine fish. It is unusually palatable to cats, which is much of why it is used.
ing_tuna.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and because animals find it very appealing.
ing_tuna.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and prefers limited exposure because of mercury concerns in some contexts. Its allergen risk is low for dogs but high for cats.

ing_apples.whatItIs: A fruit, used without the core. It supplies fibre and vitamins.
ing_apples.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and vitamins.
ing_apples.whatToWatchFor: Note: That seeds should be removed, as they contain amygdalin.

ing_brewer's_yeast.whatItIs: A yeast left over from beer brewing, dried for use as an ingredient. It carries B vitamins and a savoury flavour.
ing_brewer's_yeast.whyItsHere: Included as a source of B vitamins and to make the food taste better.
ing_brewer's_yeast.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_lamb.whatItIs: Meat from sheep. It is often chosen as a novel protein — one an animal is less likely to have eaten before.
ing_lamb.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option for animals reacting to more common meats.
ing_lamb.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts lamb's allergen risk at low to medium. Its value as a novel protein depends on the animal not having been exposed to it already.

ing_meat_by_products.whatItIs: Parts of the animal other than skeletal meat, chiefly organs. The label term does not say which animal or which parts.
ing_meat_by_products.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source; organ tissue is nutrient-dense.
ing_meat_by_products.whatToWatchFor: Because neither the animal nor the parts are named, our data puts its allergen risk at medium and you cannot tell from the label what is in it.

ing_magnesium_sulfate.whatItIs: A mineral salt, the same compound as Epsom salt, used here as a magnesium source.
ing_magnesium_sulfate.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its magnesium requirement.

ing_wheat_gluten.whatItIs: The concentrated protein fraction of wheat, separated from the starch. It is both a protein source and a binder.
ing_wheat_gluten.whyItsHere: Included to raise the protein content and to hold the food together.
ing_wheat_gluten.whatToWatchFor: Our data describes wheat gluten as a common allergen in some pets and puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_inulin.whatItIs: A soluble fibre found in plants such as chicory. It is not digested by the animal but is fermented by gut bacteria.
ing_inulin.whyItsHere: Included as a prebiotic fibre feeding the gut's own bacteria.

ing_powdered_cellulose.whatItIs: Purified plant fibre, ground to a powder. Our data describes it as non-digestible and notes its use in weight management formulas.
ing_powdered_cellulose.whyItsHere: Included as insoluble fibre and as a low-calorie filler that adds bulk without adding energy.

ing_pea_protein.whatItIs: The protein fraction of peas, concentrated by separating it from the starch and fibre.
ing_pea_protein.whyItsHere: Included to raise the protein content of the food using a plant source.

ing_turmeric.whatItIs: A yellow root spice. Our data associates it with an anti-inflammatory role.
ing_turmeric.whyItsHere: Included for that anti-inflammatory association, and it also contributes colour.
ing_turmeric.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation, and notes its low bioavailability unless paired with black pepper or fat.

ing_sodium_tripolyphosphate.whatItIs: A synthesised phosphate salt. It holds water in the product and is also used against tartar build-up.
ing_sodium_tripolyphosphate.whyItsHere: Added to retain moisture and, per our data, for dental health.

ing_wheat_flour.whatItIs: Ground wheat, used as a carbohydrate source and to bind the food together.
ing_wheat_flour.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and as a binder.
ing_wheat_flour.whatToWatchFor: Note: Wheat flour contains gluten and is a common allergen in some pets, putting its allergen risk at medium.

ing_brewers_rice.whatItIs: The small broken fragments of rice left over from milling. Our data describes them as highly digestible but lower in fibre than whole rice.
ing_brewers_rice.whyItsHere: Included as an easily digestible carbohydrate source.

ing_carrageenan.whatItIs: A gelling agent extracted from red algae, used mainly in wet food to set its texture.
ing_carrageenan.whyItsHere: Added as a gelling agent, giving canned food its consistency.
ing_carrageenan.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution and notes that some owners avoid it because of gastrointestinal sensitivity.

ing_parsley.whatItIs: A herb, used in small amounts. It is associated with freshening breath.
ing_parsley.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and says to avoid large amounts, singling out spring parsley for pregnant pets.

ing_egg.whatItIs: Whole egg, a complete protein that also helps bind the other ingredients.
ing_egg.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and as a binder.
ing_egg.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts egg's allergen risk at medium.

ing_canola_oil.whatItIs: Oil pressed from rapeseed, used as a fat source.
ing_canola_oil.whyItsHere: Included as a source of dietary fat and energy.

ing_copper_amino_acid_chelate.whatItIs: Copper bound to glycine rather than supplied as an inorganic salt. Our data describes this form as having superior absorption.
ing_copper_amino_acid_chelate.whyItsHere: Added as a highly absorbable copper source.

ing_coconut_oil.whatItIs: Oil from coconut flesh, notable for its medium-chain triglycerides. It is also used on skin and coat.
ing_coconut_oil.whyItsHere: Included as a fat source and, per our data, as a skin conditioner.
ing_coconut_oil.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation, noting it is high in saturated fat and should be used sparingly when fed.

ing_corn.whatItIs: A cereal grain, minimally processed. It supplies carbohydrate and linoleic acid, an essential fatty acid.
ing_corn.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and for its linoleic acid.
ing_corn.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe for most rather than simply safe, which allows for individual sensitivities.

ing_potato_starch.whatItIs: Starch separated from potatoes. Our data describes it as a grain-free starch used in limited-ingredient diets.
ing_potato_starch.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and to thicken or bind the food.

ing_l_lysine.whatItIs: An essential amino acid, added in synthesised form. Note: It is often supplemented in grain-based diets.
ing_l_lysine.whyItsHere: Added to top up an amino acid that plant-heavy recipes can run short of.

ing_phosphoric_acid.whatItIs: A synthesised acid used to adjust how acidic the food is.
ing_phosphoric_acid.whyItsHere: Added as a pH adjuster, keeping the recipe in its intended acidity range.

ing_chickpeas.whatItIs: A pulse, used whole or ground. It contributes both fibre and plant protein.
ing_chickpeas.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and plant protein.

ing_pea_fiber.whatItIs: Insoluble fibre from pea hulls. Our data associates it with digestive health.
ing_pea_fiber.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source adding bulk to the diet.

ing_zinc_oxide.whatItIs: A synthesised zinc compound used on skin rather than in food, where it blocks sun.
ing_zinc_oxide.whyItsHere: Included in topical products for sun protection.
ing_zinc_oxide.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes zinc oxide is toxic if ingested in large amounts, and to avoid applying it where an animal can lick, such as the nose. It is rated caution.

ing_tomato_pomace.whatItIs: The dried pulp, skin and seed left after pressing tomatoes. Our data describes it as rich in lycopene and fibre.
ing_tomato_pomace.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source that also contributes antioxidants.

ing_lactic_acid.whatItIs: An acid produced by fermentation, used to lower pH.
ing_lactic_acid.whyItsHere: Added as an acidifier and preservative.

ing_iron_amino_acid_chelate.whatItIs: Iron bound to glycine rather than supplied as an inorganic salt. Our data describes this form as having superior absorption.
ing_iron_amino_acid_chelate.whyItsHere: Added as a highly absorbable iron source.

ing_lecithin.whatItIs: A fatty substance derived from plants or eggs. It lets fat and water mix, which is what makes it an emulsifier.
ing_lecithin.whyItsHere: Added to keep fats evenly distributed; our data also associates it with brain health.

ing_green_tea_extract.whatItIs: An extract of green tea leaves. Our data describes it as rich in polyphenols and notes its FDA GRAS status.
ing_green_tea_extract.whyItsHere: Added as a natural antioxidant and preservative.

ing_zinc_amino_acid_chelate.whatItIs: Zinc bound to glycine rather than supplied as an inorganic salt. Our data describes this form as having superior absorption.
ing_zinc_amino_acid_chelate.whyItsHere: Added as a highly absorbable zinc source.

ing_soybean_meal.whatItIs: The protein-rich meal left after oil is pressed from soybeans.
ing_soybean_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein source, raising the protein content of the food.
ing_soybean_meal.whatToWatchFor: Some pets may be allergic. Rated safe for most rather than simply safe, with an allergen risk of medium.

ing_duck.whatItIs: Poultry meat, often chosen as a novel protein — one an animal is less likely to have met before.
ing_duck.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.
ing_duck.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts duck's allergen risk at low to medium. Its value as a novel protein depends on the animal not having eaten it before.

ing_lentils.whatItIs: A pulse, used whole or split, contributing fibre and plant protein.
ing_lentils.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and plant protein.

ing_vitamin_c.whatItIs: Ascorbic acid, added in synthesised form. It acts as an antioxidant.
ing_vitamin_c.whyItsHere: Included as an added antioxidant nutrient.
ing_vitamin_c.whatToWatchFor: Note: Dogs and cats make their own vitamin C, so supplementation is rarely needed.

ing_vegetable_oil.whatItIs: A generic label term for plant-based oil. It does not say which plant the oil came from.
ing_vegetable_oil.whyItsHere: Included as a fat and energy source.
ing_vegetable_oil.whatToWatchFor: Because the plant is not named, you cannot tell from the label what the oil is; our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_fos.whatItIs: Fructooligosaccharides — short chains of fruit sugars that the animal does not digest but gut bacteria ferment.
ing_fos.whyItsHere: Included as a prebiotic fibre feeding the gut's own bacteria.

ing_pork.whatItIs: Meat from pigs, used as the main protein in the recipe.
ing_pork.whyItsHere: Included as the primary protein source for the diet.
ing_pork.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts pork's allergen risk at medium.

ing_smoke_flavor.whatItIs: A flavouring condensed from wood smoke. Note: Its FDA GRAS status.
ing_smoke_flavor.whyItsHere: Added to give the food a smoked flavour animals find appealing.

ing_broccoli.whatItIs: A cruciferous vegetable, used minimally processed, contributing fibre and vitamins.
ing_broccoli.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and vitamins.
ing_broccoli.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation, noting it can cause gas and suggesting it be kept to a small share of the diet.

ing_beet_pulp.whatItIs: The fibrous material left after sugar is extracted from beets. It is a moderately fermentable fibre.
ing_beet_pulp.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source, associated in our data with stool quality.

ing_tapioca.whatItIs: Starch from the cassava root, used to bind the food together.
ing_tapioca.whyItsHere: Included as a binding starch and carbohydrate source.

ing_gelatin.whatItIs: Protein extracted from animal collagen. It sets into a gel on cooling, which is what makes it useful in wet food and chews.
ing_gelatin.whyItsHere: Included as a gelling agent that also contributes protein.

ing_soy_flour.whatItIs: Ground soybeans, used both for their protein and to bind the recipe.
ing_soy_flour.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein source and as a binder.
ing_soy_flour.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts soy flour's allergen risk at medium.

ing_pea_starch.whatItIs: Starch separated from peas. Our data describes it as a grain-free, highly digestible starch.
ing_pea_starch.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and as a binder.

ing_glucosamine_hydrochloride.whatItIs: A compound found in cartilage, added as a supplement. Our data describes this salt form as the more bioavailable one.
ing_glucosamine_hydrochloride.whyItsHere: Included as a joint health supplement.

ing_menhaden.whatItIs: A small oily marine fish, used rendered into fish meal — a concentrated protein.
ing_menhaden.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated fish protein source.

ing_heart.whatItIs: Cardiac muscle, an organ meat. It is a notably rich natural source of taurine.
ing_heart.whyItsHere: Included as an organ meat, particularly for its taurine content.
ing_heart.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts heart's allergen risk at medium.

ing_corn_gluten_meal.whatItIs: The concentrated protein fraction of corn, separated from the starch.
ing_corn_gluten_meal.whyItsHere: Included to raise the protein content of the food using a plant source.

ing_caramel_color.whatItIs: A colouring made by heating sugars. It changes how the food looks and nothing else.
ing_caramel_color.whyItsHere: Added purely for colour, which matters to the person buying rather than the animal eating.
ing_caramel_color.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution. It has no nutritional benefit, and some types may contain 4-MEI.

ing_potassium_sorbate.whatItIs: A synthesised salt widely used to stop mould growing.
ing_potassium_sorbate.whyItsHere: Added as a mould inhibitor, extending how long the food keeps.

ing_kale.whatItIs: A leafy cruciferous vegetable contributing antioxidants and fibre.
ing_kale.whyItsHere: Included as a source of antioxidants and fibre.
ing_kale.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and notes it can cause gas in large amounts.

ing_soybean_oil.whatItIs: Oil pressed and refined from soybeans, a source of omega-6 fats.
ing_soybean_oil.whyItsHere: Included as a fat source, described in our data as a common vegetable oil in pet food.
ing_soybean_oil.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts soybean oil's allergen risk at medium.

ing_beta_carotene.whatItIs: An orange plant pigment that acts as an antioxidant and, in some animals, converts to vitamin A.
ing_beta_carotene.whyItsHere: Included as an antioxidant and as a vitamin A precursor.
ing_beta_carotene.whatToWatchFor: Note: That dogs convert beta-carotene to vitamin A but cats cannot, so it is not a vitamin A source for a cat.

ing_rice_flour.whatItIs: Ground rice. Our data describes it as gluten-free and easily digestible.
ing_rice_flour.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and as a binder.

ing_whitefish.whatItIs: A general term for mild white-fleshed fish. The label does not say which species.
ing_whitefish.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source in the recipe.
ing_whitefish.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium, and the species is not named on the label.

ing_wheat.whatItIs: A cereal grain supplying carbohydrate, also used to bind the food together.
ing_wheat.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and as a binder.
ing_wheat.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe for most rather than simply safe, and puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_chondroitin.whatItIs: A component of cartilage, added as a supplement. Note: It is often paired with glucosamine.
ing_chondroitin.whyItsHere: Included as a joint health supplement.

ing_glycine.whatItIs: The simplest amino acid, added in synthesised form. It is a major component of collagen.
ing_glycine.whyItsHere: Added as an amino acid contributing to the diet's protein profile.

ing_l_threonine.whatItIs: An essential amino acid, added in synthesised form. Note: Its importance for protein synthesis.
ing_l_threonine.whyItsHere: Added to balance the amino acid profile of the finished diet.

ing_locust_bean_gum.whatItIs: A thickener made from carob seeds. It swells in water to give body to a mixture.
ing_locust_bean_gum.whyItsHere: Added to thicken the food and hold its texture.

ing_potato_protein.whatItIs: The protein fraction of potatoes, concentrated by separating it from the starch. Note: It as a grain-free option.
ing_potato_protein.whyItsHere: Included to raise protein content using a plant source.

ing_calcium_propionate.whatItIs: A synthesised calcium salt. Note: Its FDA GRAS status and common use in baked treats.
ing_calcium_propionate.whyItsHere: Added to stop mould growing, extending shelf life.

ing_yeast_extract.whatItIs: Yeast broken down to release its savoury compounds. Our data describes it as a natural source of umami flavour and B vitamins.
ing_yeast_extract.whyItsHere: Added to make the food taste better; it also contributes B vitamins.

ing_magnesium.whatItIs: An essential mineral, added in synthetic form. Muscles and nerves depend on it to work properly.
ing_magnesium.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its magnesium requirement.
ing_magnesium.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to monitor magnesium in cats with urinary issues.

ing_menhaden_fish_meal.whatItIs: Menhaden fish rendered and dried into a concentrated meal, described in our data as a common fish meal source in pet food.
ing_menhaden_fish_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source that also supplies omega-3.
ing_menhaden_fish_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_corn_starch.whatItIs: Pure starch separated from corn. Our data describes it as a highly digestible energy source.
ing_corn_starch.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and to thicken the food.

ing_peanut_butter.whatItIs: Ground peanuts, used mainly in dog treats and for hiding medication. Our data lists it for dog products.
ing_peanut_butter.whyItsHere: Included as a flavour animals find highly appealing, often for training treats.
ing_peanut_butter.whatToWatchFor: Our data states peanut butter must be xylitol-free and to check the ingredients carefully, and rates it safe in moderation. Xylitol is a separate ingredient with its own emergency-level rule.

ing_cassia_gum.whatItIs: A thickener made from cassia seeds. Note: It is FDA approved for pet food use.
ing_cassia_gum.whyItsHere: Added to thicken the food and set its texture.

ing_herring.whatItIs: An oily marine fish used as a protein source, naturally rich in omega-3.
ing_herring.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and as an omega-3 source.
ing_herring.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts herring's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_red_40.whatItIs: A synthetic dye, also called Allura Red AC. Its only effect on the food is colour.
ing_red_40.whyItsHere: Added purely for visual appeal — to the person buying the food, not the animal eating it.
ing_red_40.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes Red 40 has no nutritional value and that some animals may show sensitivity. It is FDA approved but rated caution here.

ing_yellow_5.whatItIs: A synthetic dye, also called tartrazine. Its only effect on the food is colour.
ing_yellow_5.whyItsHere: Added purely for visual appeal rather than for the animal's benefit.
ing_yellow_5.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes Yellow 5 has no nutritional value and that some animals may show sensitivity. It is FDA approved but rated caution here.

ing_selenium_yeast.whatItIs: Selenium grown into yeast so it comes bound to organic compounds rather than as a plain salt.
ing_selenium_yeast.whyItsHere: Added as a selenium source; our data describes this form as better absorbed than inorganic selenium.

ing_titanium_dioxide.whatItIs: A synthetic white pigment. It makes food look whiter or brighter and does nothing else.
ing_titanium_dioxide.whyItsHere: Added purely as a whitening colourant.
ing_titanium_dioxide.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes titanium dioxide has no nutritional value and has been banned as a food additive in some countries. It is rated caution.

ing_monocalcium_phosphate.whatItIs: A synthesised mineral supplying calcium and phosphorus, and the most soluble of the calcium phosphates.
ing_monocalcium_phosphate.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its calcium and phosphorus requirements.

ing_green_beans.whatItIs: A vegetable pod, used whole or cut. It adds bulk and fibre for very few calories.
ing_green_beans.whyItsHere: Included as a low-calorie fibre source.

ing_sorbic_acid.whatItIs: A synthesised preservative. Note: Its FDA GRAS status and that it inhibits mould and yeast.
ing_sorbic_acid.whyItsHere: Added to stop mould and yeast growing in the food.

ing_pearled_barley.whatItIs: Barley with the hull polished off, which makes it cook faster but removes some of the fibre.

ing_vitamin_d.whatItIs: Cholecalciferol, a fat-soluble vitamin added in synthetic form. It governs how calcium is absorbed and used.
ing_vitamin_d.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient supporting calcium absorption and bone health.
ing_vitamin_d.whatToWatchFor: Our data describes vitamin D as essential but toxic in excess, and says to monitor supplementation. Being fat-soluble, it accumulates.

ing_garlic.whatItIs: A bulb from the allium family, used for flavour. Our data describes its risk as dose dependent.
ing_garlic.whyItsHere: Included as a flavouring, to make the food more appealing.
ing_garlic.whatToWatchFor: Rated caution for dogs and toxic for cats, and the safety guidance says to prefer avoiding it unless clearly formulated safely. Listed symptoms include gastrointestinal irritation, anemia, weakness, pale gums, elevated heart rate and collapse.

ing_l_tryptophan.whatItIs: An essential amino acid added in synthesised form. It is the precursor the body uses to make serotonin.
ing_l_tryptophan.whyItsHere: Added to balance the amino acid profile; our data associates it with calming and sleep.

ing_bha.whatItIs: Butylated hydroxyanisole, a synthetic antioxidant preservative.
ing_bha.whyItsHere: Added to stop fats going rancid, extending shelf life.
ing_bha.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes some studies suggest potential carcinogenic effects, and that many premium foods avoid it. It is rated caution.

ing_chia_seeds.whatItIs: Small seeds from the chia plant. Note: Their plant-based omega-3 and high fibre content.
ing_chia_seeds.whyItsHere: Included as a plant omega-3 source and for fibre.

ing_soy_protein_concentrate.whatItIs: Soy protein concentrated by removing most of the carbohydrate.
ing_soy_protein_concentrate.whyItsHere: Included to raise the protein content of the food using a plant source.
ing_soy_protein_concentrate.whatToWatchFor: Our data describes soy protein concentrate as a common allergen in some pets and puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_marigold_extract.whatItIs: An extract of marigold flowers, and the usual commercial source of lutein and zeaxanthin.
ing_marigold_extract.whyItsHere: Included as a lutein source, associated in our data with vision support.

ing_pork_fat.whatItIs: Rendered fat from pigs, also known as lard. Our data describes it as a calorie-dense energy source.
ing_pork_fat.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated energy source.

ing_herring_oil.whatItIs: Oil from herring, rich in the long-chain omega-3 fats EPA and DHA.
ing_herring_oil.whyItsHere: Included as an omega-3 source, associated in our data with skin, coat and cognitive health.

ing_green_lipped_mussel.whatItIs: A shellfish from New Zealand. Note: It naturally contains glucosamine and chondroitin.
ing_green_lipped_mussel.whyItsHere: Included for joint support and as an omega-3 source.

ing_ginger.whatItIs: A root spice, associated in our data with digestion and easing nausea.
ing_ginger.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive aid, associated in our data with easing nausea.
ing_ginger.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation rather than simply safe.

ing_sodium_hexametaphosphate.whatItIs: A synthesised phosphate salt used on the surface of kibble and treats.
ing_sodium_hexametaphosphate.whyItsHere: Added to help reduce tartar build-up on the teeth.

ing_potato.whatItIs: A starchy tuber used as a carbohydrate source.
ing_potato.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source in the recipe.
ing_potato.whatToWatchFor: Note: Potato must be cooked and that green parts are toxic.

ing_yellow_6.whatItIs: A synthetic dye, also called Sunset Yellow FCF. Its only effect on the food is colour.
ing_yellow_6.whyItsHere: Added purely for visual appeal rather than for the animal's benefit.
ing_yellow_6.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes Yellow 6 has no nutritional value and that some animals may show sensitivity. It is FDA approved but rated caution here.

ing_hydrolyzed_yeast.whatItIs: Yeast broken down into smaller fragments. Note: It as a source of beta-glucans and mannan-oligosaccharides.
ing_hydrolyzed_yeast.whyItsHere: Included as a prebiotic, associated in our data with immune support.

ing_psyllium_husk.whatItIs: The husk of psyllium seed, a concentrated soluble fibre that forms a gel with water.
ing_psyllium_husk.whyItsHere: Included as a soluble fibre source, associated in our data with digestive regularity.

ing_beef_tallow.whatItIs: Rendered beef fat, described in our data as a traditional fat source.
ing_beef_tallow.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated energy source and to make the food more palatable.
ing_beef_tallow.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts beef tallow's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_bananas.whatItIs: A fruit used in small amounts, contributing potassium and fibre.
ing_bananas.whyItsHere: Included as a source of potassium and fibre, often in treats.
ing_bananas.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation, noting they are high in sugar and should be used sparingly.

ing_blue_2.whatItIs: A synthetic dye, also called indigotine. Its only effect on the food is colour.
ing_blue_2.whyItsHere: Added purely for visual appeal rather than for the animal's benefit.
ing_blue_2.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes Blue 2 has no nutritional value and that some animals may show sensitivity. It is FDA approved but rated caution here.

ing_kidney.whatItIs: Organ meat, dense in micronutrients. The label does not usually say which animal it came from.
ing_kidney.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense organ meat.
ing_kidney.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts kidney's allergen risk at medium.

ing_iron_oxide.whatItIs: A mineral pigment giving red, yellow or black colour. Note: It is an FDA approved colour additive.
ing_iron_oxide.whyItsHere: Added as a colourant, mainly so the product looks like what it is meant to resemble.

ing_turkey_liver.whatItIs: Liver from turkey, an organ meat that is dense in micronutrients.
ing_turkey_liver.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense organ meat and for palatability.
ing_turkey_liver.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts turkey liver's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_shrimp.whatItIs: A small shellfish, used for its protein and its strong flavour.
ing_shrimp.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and to make the food more appealing.
ing_shrimp.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts shrimp's allergen risk at medium.

ing_millet.whatItIs: A small gluten-free cereal grain used as a carbohydrate source.
ing_millet.whyItsHere: Included as a gluten-free carbohydrate source.

ing_whitefish_meal.whatItIs: White fish rendered and dried into a concentrated meal. The species is not named on the label.
ing_whitefish_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_whitefish_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium, and the fish species is not identified.

ing_oat_fiber.whatItIs: Insoluble fibre from oats. Our data describes it as a low-calorie fibre supporting digestive health.
ing_oat_fiber.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source adding bulk without much energy.

ing_mackerel.whatItIs: An oily marine fish used for its protein and its omega-3 content.
ing_mackerel.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and as an omega-3 source.
ing_mackerel.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts mackerel's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_lung.whatItIs: Organ meat from the respiratory tract. The label does not usually say which animal.
ing_lung.whyItsHere: Included as an organ meat contributing protein.
ing_lung.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts lung's allergen risk at medium, and the source animal is not named.

ing_poultry_by_products.whatItIs: The clean non-meat parts of poultry carcasses, unrendered. Our data describes them as chiefly organ tissue.
ing_poultry_by_products.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source; organ tissue is nutrient-dense.
ing_poultry_by_products.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts the allergen risk at medium. The label does not say which bird or which parts.

ing_meat_and_bone_meal.whatItIs: A rendered and dried product that includes bone as well as meat, so it supplies calcium alongside protein.
ing_meat_and_bone_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a combined protein and calcium source.
ing_meat_and_bone_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium. Neither the animal nor the parts are named on the label.

ing_oat_flour.whatItIs: Ground whole oats. Note: It as a good source of beta-glucan fibre.
ing_oat_flour.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source that also contributes fibre.

ing_sorbitol.whatItIs: A sugar alcohol used as a sweetener, derived from natural sources.
ing_sorbitol.whyItsHere: Added to sweeten the product without using sugar.
ing_sorbitol.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes sorbitol can cause gastrointestinal upset and diarrhoea, and describe it as less dangerous than xylitol but best avoided. It is rated caution.

ing_lamb_liver.whatItIs: Liver from lamb, an organ meat dense in micronutrients.
ing_lamb_liver.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense organ meat.

ing_rice_bran.whatItIs: The outer layer of the rice grain, removed during milling. Note: It is rich in B vitamins and fibre.
ing_rice_bran.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source that also carries B vitamins.

ing_sardines.whatItIs: A small oily fish, used whole. It is naturally rich in omega-3.
ing_sardines.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and as an omega-3 source.
ing_sardines.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts sardines' allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_poultry_fat.whatItIs: Fat rendered from poultry. Our data describes it as highly palatable and a good source of linoleic acid.
ing_poultry_fat.whyItsHere: Included as an energy source and to make the food more appealing.
ing_poultry_fat.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium. The label says poultry rather than naming the bird.

ing_celery.whatItIs: A crisp vegetable stalk, very low in calories.
ing_celery.whyItsHere: Included as a low-calorie ingredient, often in treats.
ing_celery.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to cut celery into small pieces to prevent choking.

ing_quinoa.whatItIs: A seed used like a grain. It is one of the few plant foods that supplies a complete protein.
ing_quinoa.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source that also contributes complete protein.
ing_quinoa.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to rinse quinoa well before cooking to remove saponins.

ing_miscanthus_grass.whatItIs: A fibrous grass, ground for use as a fibre source. Note: It as a sustainable one.
ing_miscanthus_grass.whyItsHere: Included as an insoluble fibre source supporting digestive health.

ing_agar_agar.whatItIs: A gelling agent extracted from seaweed. It sets firmer than gelatin and is plant-based.
ing_agar_agar.whyItsHere: Added as a gelling agent, giving wet food its set texture.

ing_venison.whatItIs: Deer meat, commonly chosen as a novel protein — one an animal is unlikely to have eaten before.
ing_venison.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.

ing_peppermint_oil.whatItIs: An essential oil distilled from peppermint.
ing_peppermint_oil.whyItsHere: Included as an essential oil, typically for scent or flavour.
ing_peppermint_oil.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: it can cause liver damage, difficulty breathing and CNS depression. Our data states cats lack the enzymes to metabolise it, so any amount is a concern. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea and CNS depression.

ing_olive_oil.whatItIs: Oil pressed from olives, used as a fat source.
ing_olive_oil.whyItsHere: Included as a fat source, associated in our data with coat health.
ing_olive_oil.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and says to use it sparingly because it is high in calories.

ing_sunflower_lecithin.whatItIs: An emulsifier from sunflower seeds. Our data describes it as a non-GMO alternative to soy lecithin.
ing_sunflower_lecithin.whyItsHere: Added to keep fats and water mixed; our data also associates it with brain health.

ing_chamomile.whatItIs: A flowering herb, used dried. It is traditionally used as a soothing botanical.
ing_chamomile.whyItsHere: Included as a soothing botanical ingredient.

ing_cod.whatItIs: A mild white marine fish, lean and low in fat, used as a protein source.
ing_cod.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source in the recipe.

ing_sodium_nitrite.whatItIs: A synthesised salt used to preserve meat and keep it looking pink rather than grey.
ing_sodium_nitrite.whyItsHere: Added as a preservative and to fix the colour of meat products.
ing_sodium_nitrite.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes sodium nitrite can form carcinogenic nitrosamines and is generally best avoided in pet food. It is rated caution.

ing_oat_groats.whatItIs: Whole oat kernels with only the inedible hull removed, so the grain stays intact.
ing_oat_groats.whyItsHere: Included as a whole-grain carbohydrate source.

ing_chicken_gizzard.whatItIs: A muscular part of the bird's digestive tract. Our data describes it as a lean muscle organ.
ing_chicken_gizzard.whyItsHere: Included as an organ meat contributing lean protein.
ing_chicken_gizzard.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, the same sensitivity that applies to chicken generally.

ing_chicken_by_products.whatItIs: Parts of the chicken other than skeletal meat. Our data lists necks, feet, undeveloped eggs and intestines.
ing_chicken_by_products.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source; these parts are nutrient-dense.
ing_chicken_by_products.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts the allergen risk at medium, and the exact mix of parts is not stated on the label.

ing_dried_whey.whatItIs: The protein fraction of milk left after cheese-making, spray dried to a powder.
ing_dried_whey.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and it adds a milky flavour.
ing_dried_whey.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts dried whey's allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_pomegranate.whatItIs: A fruit rich in polyphenols. Note: Its ellagic acid content.
ing_pomegranate.whyItsHere: Included as an antioxidant source, associated in our data with immune health.

ing_tripe.whatItIs: The stomach lining of a ruminant. Our data singles out green tripe as especially beneficial.
ing_tripe.whyItsHere: Included for its digestive enzymes and naturally occurring probiotics.
ing_tripe.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts tripe's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_modified_food_starch.whatItIs: Starch that has been chemically or physically altered to change how it behaves. Note: Its FDA GRAS status.
ing_modified_food_starch.whyItsHere: Added to thicken the food and control its texture.

ing_flaxseed_oil.whatItIs: Oil cold-pressed from flaxseed, a plant source of the short-chain omega-3 ALA.
ing_flaxseed_oil.whyItsHere: Included as a plant omega-3 source.
ing_flaxseed_oil.whatToWatchFor: Note: This is plant-based omega-3 that requires conversion in the body, unlike the fats in fish oil.

ing_propylene_glycol.whatItIs: A synthesised humectant that holds moisture in soft foods. Our data lists it for dog products.
ing_propylene_glycol.whyItsHere: Added to keep semi-moist food soft and to help preserve it.
ing_propylene_glycol.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats and the FDA has banned it in cat food, because any amount causes hemolytic anemia. Listed symptoms include Heinz body anemia, weakness and lethargy. It is recorded as safe for dogs at food-grade levels.

ing_papaya.whatItIs: A tropical fruit containing enzymes that break down protein.
ing_papaya.whyItsHere: Included for its digestive enzymes and fibre.
ing_papaya.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to remove the seeds.

ing_coconut.whatItIs: The flesh of the coconut, notable for its medium-chain triglycerides.
ing_coconut.whyItsHere: Included as a fat source and for flavour.
ing_coconut.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation, noting it is high in fat and should be used sparingly.

ing_butternut_squash.whatItIs: A winter squash, cooked before use. It supplies fibre and vitamin A.
ing_butternut_squash.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and vitamin A.

ing_ocean_fish_meal.whatItIs: A mix of marine fish, rendered and dried. Note: It as a good source of omega-3.
ing_ocean_fish_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated fish protein source.
ing_ocean_fish_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium. The label does not identify which fish are in the mix.

ing_animal_digest.whatItIs: Animal tissue broken down with enzymes into a concentrated savoury liquid, sprayed onto kibble. Note: The source is unspecified.
ing_animal_digest.whyItsHere: Added purely to make the food taste better — it is the main reason plain kibble is palatable.
ing_animal_digest.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and because the source animal is unspecified you cannot tell what it was made from.

ing_cheese.whatItIs: A fermented dairy product. Note: It is lower in lactose than milk.
ing_cheese.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and fat, and because animals find it very appealing.
ing_cheese.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and puts its allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_cobalt.whatItIs: A trace mineral. Note: It is commonly added as cobalt carbonate or cobalt sulfate.
ing_cobalt.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts; it is the atom at the centre of vitamin B12.

ing_soy_protein_isolate.whatItIs: The most concentrated soy protein fraction, with nearly all carbohydrate and fat removed.
ing_soy_protein_isolate.whyItsHere: Included to raise the protein content of the food using a plant source.
ing_soy_protein_isolate.whatToWatchFor: Our data describes soy protein isolate as a common allergen in some pets and puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_sorghum.whatItIs: A gluten-free cereal grain used as a carbohydrate source.
ing_sorghum.whyItsHere: Included as a gluten-free carbohydrate source.

ing_canola_meal.whatItIs: What remains after oil is pressed from canola seed. Our data describes it as moderate in protein.
ing_canola_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.

ing_corn_flour.whatItIs: Finely ground corn. Note: It is gluten-free.
ing_corn_flour.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts corn flour's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_alfalfa_meal.whatItIs: Alfalfa dried and ground. It contributes fibre and chlorophyll.
ing_alfalfa_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source in the recipe.

ing_alfalfa.whatItIs: A legume plant, used as forage and dried for feed. It carries fibre along with vitamins and minerals.
ing_alfalfa.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source that also contributes vitamins and minerals.

ing_rabbit.whatItIs: Rabbit meat, commonly chosen as a novel protein — one an animal is unlikely to have eaten before.
ing_rabbit.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.

ing_white_rice.whatItIs: Rice with the bran and germ milled away, leaving mostly starch. That makes it gentler on digestion but lower in fibre than brown rice.
ing_white_rice.whyItsHere: Included as an easily digestible carbohydrate source.

ing_dried_coconut.whatItIs: Dehydrated coconut flesh, supplying fibre and medium-chain triglycerides.
ing_dried_coconut.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source that also contributes fat.
ing_dried_coconut.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation rather than simply safe.

ing_vitamin_b12.whatItIs: Cyanocobalamin, an essential B vitamin added in synthetic form.
ing_vitamin_b12.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in red blood cell formation.

ing_blackberries.whatItIs: A dark berry used whole or dried, contributing antioxidants and fibre.
ing_blackberries.whyItsHere: Included as a source of antioxidants and fibre.

ing_squash.whatItIs: A gourd vegetable, cooked before use, contributing fibre and vitamins.
ing_squash.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and vitamins.

ing_raspberries.whatItIs: A soft red berry contributing antioxidants and fibre.
ing_raspberries.whyItsHere: Included as a source of antioxidants and fibre.
ing_raspberries.whatToWatchFor: Note: Raspberries naturally contain xylitol in small amounts and rates them safe in moderation on that basis.

ing_apple_pomace.whatItIs: The dried pulp left after pressing apples. Note: It contains pectin.
ing_apple_pomace.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source with prebiotic properties.

ing_corn_germ_meal.whatItIs: What remains after oil is extracted from the corn germ. It carries both protein and fibre.
ing_corn_germ_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a protein and fibre source.

ing_gum_arabic.whatItIs: Hardened sap from the acacia tree, dissolved for use as a stabiliser.
ing_gum_arabic.whyItsHere: Added to keep the mixture stable and stop ingredients separating.

ing_peanuts.whatItIs: Legume seeds used mainly in dog treats. Note: Cats are rarely interested. Our data lists it for dog products.
ing_peanuts.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and for flavour in treats.
ing_peanuts.whatToWatchFor: Only unsalted peanuts with no xylitol. Rated safe in moderation, with an allergen risk of low to medium.

ing_l_tyrosine.whatItIs: An amino acid added in synthesised form. Note: It is a precursor to dopamine and thyroid hormones.
ing_l_tyrosine.whyItsHere: Added to balance the amino acid profile of the finished diet.

ing_animal_liver.whatItIs: Liver, described in our data as unspecified mammalian liver — the label does not say which animal.
ing_animal_liver.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense organ meat.
ing_animal_liver.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and the source animal is not identified.

ing_wheat_bran.whatItIs: The outer layer of the wheat kernel, separated during milling. It is a concentrated insoluble fibre.
ing_wheat_bran.whyItsHere: Included as an insoluble fibre source adding bulk.
ing_wheat_bran.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts wheat bran's allergen risk at medium.

ing_bison.whatItIs: Meat from bison, commonly chosen as a novel protein.
ing_bison.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.

ing_ocean_fish.whatItIs: A generic label term covering various ocean fish species. It does not say which.
ing_ocean_fish.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source in the recipe.
ing_ocean_fish.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and the species is not identified on the label.

ing_turkey_heart.whatItIs: Cardiac muscle from turkey, an organ meat that is a rich natural source of taurine.
ing_turkey_heart.whyItsHere: Included as an organ meat, particularly for its taurine.
ing_turkey_heart.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_lamb_heart.whatItIs: Cardiac muscle from lamb, an organ meat rich in taurine.
ing_lamb_heart.whyItsHere: Included as an organ meat, particularly for its taurine.

ing_bht.whatItIs: Butylated hydroxytoluene, a synthetic antioxidant preservative.
ing_bht.whyItsHere: Added to stop fats going rancid, extending shelf life.
ing_bht.whatToWatchFor: Our data and the safety guidance both raise health concerns, note some countries have restricted its use in human food, and say natural alternatives such as mixed tocopherols are preferred. It is rated caution.

ing_dried_tomato.whatItIs: Dehydrated tomato, a concentrated source of the pigment lycopene.
ing_dried_tomato.whatToWatchFor: Our data specifies ripe tomatoes only.

ing_carob_bean_gum.whatItIs: A thickener extracted from carob seeds. Note: It is the same as locust bean gum.
ing_carob_bean_gum.whyItsHere: Added to thicken the food and keep its texture stable.

ing_zucchini.whatItIs: A summer squash, mild and very low in calories.
ing_zucchini.whyItsHere: Included as a low-calorie vegetable ingredient.

ing_safflower_oil.whatItIs: Oil pressed from safflower seed. Note: It is high in linoleic acid.
ing_safflower_oil.whyItsHere: Included as an omega-6 fat source, associated with skin and coat health.

ing_pollock.whatItIs: A mild white marine fish related to cod, used as a lean protein source.
ing_pollock.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source in the recipe.

ing_paprika_color.whatItIs: Ground peppers used as a natural red-orange colourant.
ing_paprika_color.whyItsHere: Added for colour, using a spice rather than a synthetic dye.

ing_egg_white.whatItIs: The clear part of the egg. Our data describes it as a fat-free protein source.
ing_egg_white.whyItsHere: Included as lean protein and as a binder.
ing_egg_white.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts egg white's allergen risk at medium.

ing_blue_1.whatItIs: Brilliant Blue, a synthesised dye. Our data describes it as controversial.
ing_blue_1.whyItsHere: Added purely for colour rather than for the animal's benefit.
ing_blue_1.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution and described as controversial, with an allergen risk of low to medium.

ing_cod_liver_oil.whatItIs: Oil extracted from cod liver. Note: It is rich in fat-soluble vitamins as well as omega-3.
ing_cod_liver_oil.whyItsHere: Included as an omega-3 source that also supplies vitamins A and D.

ing_l_arginine.whatItIs: An amino acid added in synthesised form. Note: It is essential for cats and critical to the urea cycle.
ing_l_arginine.whyItsHere: Added to make sure the diet supplies enough arginine.

ing_wheat_middlings.whatItIs: A by-product of wheat milling. Note: It contains bran, germ and flour.
ing_wheat_middlings.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre and nutrient source.
ing_wheat_middlings.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium. What it contains varies with the milling run.

ing_rye.whatItIs: A cereal grain. Note: It contains gluten and is high in fibre.
ing_rye.whyItsHere: Included as a whole-grain carbohydrate source.
ing_rye.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts rye's allergen risk at low to medium and notes it contains gluten.

ing_avocado.whatItIs: A fatty fruit. Note: It contains persin and that some pet foods use avocado oil safely.
ing_avocado.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes persin can cause mild gastrointestinal upset and that the pit is a choking hazard. It is rated caution.

ing_corn_oil.whatItIs: Oil extracted and refined from corn, a source of omega-6 fats.
ing_corn_oil.whyItsHere: Included as a source of dietary fat and energy.
ing_corn_oil.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts corn oil's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_trout.whatItIs: A freshwater fish used as a protein source.
ing_trout.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source in the recipe.

ing_yogurt.whatItIs: Fermented milk. Note: That fermentation reduces its lactose.
ing_yogurt.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and its naturally occurring probiotics.
ing_yogurt.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts yogurt's allergen risk at low to medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_carmine.whatItIs: A red colourant extracted from cochineal insects.
ing_carmine.whyItsHere: Added for colour, from an animal rather than synthetic source.
ing_carmine.whatToWatchFor: Note: Carmine may cause reactions in sensitive animals and puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_tilapia.whatItIs: A mild freshwater fish. Our data describes it as a lean protein source.
ing_tilapia.whyItsHere: Included as a fish protein source.
ing_tilapia.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts tilapia's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_inositol.whatItIs: A compound sometimes called vitamin B8, added in synthesised form. It is part of how cell membranes are built.

ing_cheese_powder.whatItIs: Cheese dried and ground to a powder, used to coat or flavour products.
ing_cheese_powder.whyItsHere: Added to make the food taste better; animals find dairy flavours appealing.
ing_cheese_powder.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and puts its allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_duck_liver.whatItIs: Liver from duck, an organ meat dense in micronutrients.
ing_duck_liver.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense organ meat.

ing_menhaden_oil.whatItIs: Oil from menhaden, described in our data as a common fish oil in pet food.

ing_cellulose.whatItIs: Plant fibre that passes through undigested, used to add bulk.
ing_cellulose.whyItsHere: Included as insoluble fibre adding bulk to the diet.

ing_chickpea_flour.whatItIs: Ground chickpeas, contributing plant protein and helping bind the food.
ing_chickpea_flour.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein source and as a binder.

ing_l_cysteine.whatItIs: A sulfur-containing amino acid added in synthesised form. Note: It is a precursor to glutathione.
ing_l_cysteine.whyItsHere: Added to balance the amino acid profile of the finished diet.

ing_cottage_cheese.whatItIs: A fresh, high-moisture cheese, lightly processed.
ing_cottage_cheese.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source that animals find palatable.
ing_cottage_cheese.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and puts its allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_dried_potato.whatItIs: Dehydrated potato, used as a shelf-stable carbohydrate source.

ing_yucca_schidigera.whatItIs: An extract of the yucca plant. It is associated with reducing the odour of stools.
ing_yucca_schidigera.whyItsHere: Included to help reduce stool odour.

ing_dried_egg_white.whatItIs: Egg white spray dried to a powder, giving a very concentrated lean protein.
ing_dried_egg_white.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated lean protein source.
ing_dried_egg_white.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_pear.whatItIs: A fruit contributing fibre and vitamins.
ing_pear.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and vitamins.
ing_pear.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to remove the seeds and core.

ing_palm_oil.whatItIs: Oil pressed and refined from oil-palm fruit, high in saturated fat.
ing_palm_oil.whyItsHere: Included as a source of dietary fat and energy.
ing_palm_oil.whatToWatchFor: Note: Environmental concerns with how palm oil is sourced.

ing_spleen.whatItIs: An organ meat and a notably rich source of iron. The label does not say which animal.
ing_spleen.whyItsHere: Included as an organ meat and iron source.
ing_spleen.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts spleen's allergen risk at medium, and the source animal is not named.

ing_pineapple.whatItIs: A tropical fruit containing bromelain, an enzyme that breaks down protein.
ing_pineapple.whyItsHere: Included for its enzymes and vitamins.
ing_pineapple.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation. It is high in sugar, and the skin and core should be removed.

ing_crab.whatItIs: A shellfish, used cooked as a protein source in the recipe.
ing_crab.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source in the recipe.
ing_crab.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts crab's allergen risk at medium and says to remove the shell before feeding.

ing_sunflower_meal.whatItIs: What remains after oil is pressed from sunflower seed. Note: Its good fibre content.
ing_sunflower_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.

ing_quail.whatItIs: A small game bird, commonly chosen as a novel protein.
ing_quail.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.

ing_mango.whatItIs: A tropical stone fruit, used without the pit. It carries vitamins A, C and E.
ing_mango.whyItsHere: Included as a source of vitamins in fruit form.
ing_mango.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to remove the pit, which is a choking hazard.

ing_kangaroo.whatItIs: Kangaroo meat, a lean game meat commonly chosen as a novel protein.
ing_kangaroo.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.

ing_cabbage.whatItIs: A leafy cruciferous vegetable, used as a fibre source.
ing_cabbage.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source in the recipe.
ing_cabbage.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and notes it can cause gas.

ing_pectin.whatItIs: A soluble fibre found in fruit. It gels in water, which is what makes it a thickener.
ing_pectin.whyItsHere: Included as a natural thickener that also acts as soluble fibre.

ing_glucosamine.whatItIs: A compound found naturally in cartilage, added as a supplement.
ing_glucosamine.whyItsHere: Included as a joint health supplement.

ing_lamb_fat.whatItIs: Fat rendered from lamb, an energy-dense ingredient that carries flavour.
ing_lamb_fat.whyItsHere: Included as an energy source and to make the food more appealing.
ing_lamb_fat.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts lamb fat's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_goat_milk.whatItIs: Milk from goats. Note: It is often better tolerated than cow milk.
ing_goat_milk.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and fat, and for its digestibility.
ing_goat_milk.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts goat milk's allergen risk at low to medium. It is still a dairy ingredient.

ing_spelt.whatItIs: An ancient wheat variety. Note: It contains gluten and has a good nutritional profile.
ing_spelt.whyItsHere: Included as a whole-grain carbohydrate source.
ing_spelt.whatToWatchFor: Note: Spelt contains gluten and puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_mono_diglycerides.whatItIs: Fat-derived emulsifiers. Note: Their FDA GRAS status and that they help blend fat and water.
ing_mono_diglycerides.whyItsHere: Added to keep fat and water mixed rather than separating.

ing_catfish.whatItIs: A freshwater fish. Our data describes it as a good source of protein and omega fatty acids.
ing_catfish.whyItsHere: Included as a fish protein source.
ing_catfish.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts catfish's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_krill_meal.whatItIs: Krill dried and ground. Note: It is rich in astaxanthin and phospholipid omega-3s.
ing_krill_meal.whyItsHere: Included as an omega-3 source that also contributes protein.

ing_msm.whatItIs: Methylsulfonylmethane, a sulfur compound added in synthetic form.
ing_msm.whyItsHere: Included as a joint health supplement, associated in our data with an anti-inflammatory role.

ing_quail_egg.whatItIs: Eggs from quail. Our data describes them as an alternative egg source.
ing_quail_egg.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense protein, and as a less common egg option.

ing_fish_protein_concentrate.whatItIs: Fish protein that has been processed and concentrated. The species is not named.
ing_fish_protein_concentrate.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_fish_protein_concentrate.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and the fish species is not identified.

ing_probiotics.whatItIs: Live beneficial bacteria, typically Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium species.
ing_probiotics.whyItsHere: Included to support the gut microbiome and digestion.

ing_lettuce.whatItIs: A leafy salad vegetable that is mostly water. Note: Its low nutritional value.
ing_lettuce.whyItsHere: Included as a low-calorie ingredient contributing moisture.

ing_phosphorus.whatItIs: An essential mineral, added in synthetic form. It works alongside calcium in bone.
ing_phosphorus.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its phosphorus requirement.
ing_phosphorus.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to monitor phosphorus in kidney disease.

ing_navy_beans.whatItIs: A small white bean contributing plant protein and fibre.
ing_navy_beans.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.
ing_navy_beans.whatToWatchFor: Our data states navy beans must be cooked.

ing_onion_powder.whatItIs: Dehydrated onion. Note: This concentrated form is more toxic per gram than fresh onion.
ing_onion_powder.whyItsHere: Included as a flavouring in the recipe.
ing_onion_powder.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: it can cause hemolytic anemia, and the dried form is more concentrated than fresh.

ing_calcium_ascorbate.whatItIs: A buffered form of vitamin C. Our data describes it as gentler on the stomach.
ing_calcium_ascorbate.whyItsHere: Included as a vitamin C source and antioxidant.

ing_sodium_ascorbate.whatItIs: A buffered form of vitamin C that also works as a preservative.
ing_sodium_ascorbate.whyItsHere: Included as a vitamin C source and as a preservative.

ing_catnip.whatItIs: A mint-family herb. Our data describes its stimulating effect on most cats as safe and non-addictive. Our data lists it for cat products.
ing_catnip.whyItsHere: Included as an attractant and for enrichment rather than nutrition.

ing_whey.whatItIs: The liquid fraction left over from cheese making, dried for use as a protein.
ing_whey.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source in the recipe.
ing_whey.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts whey's allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_fava_beans.whatItIs: Also known as broad beans. Note: Their good protein content.
ing_fava_beans.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein source.

ing_casein.whatItIs: The main protein in milk, separated out. It digests more slowly than whey.
ing_casein.whyItsHere: Included as a slow-release protein source.
ing_casein.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts casein's allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_hydrolyzed_chicken.whatItIs: Chicken protein broken into fragments small enough that the immune system is less likely to react. Note: Its use in prescription diets.
ing_hydrolyzed_chicken.whyItsHere: Included as a hypoallergenic protein source for animals reacting to intact proteins.

ing_asparagus.whatItIs: A vegetable stalk contributing fibre and vitamins.
ing_asparagus.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and vitamins.
ing_asparagus.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to cook asparagus before feeding, as raw is tough to digest.

ing_erythritol.whatItIs: A sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener.
ing_erythritol.whyItsHere: Added to sweeten the product without using sugar.
ing_erythritol.whatToWatchFor: Our data and the safety guidance both describe erythritol as less toxic than xylitol but still best avoided for dogs. It is rated caution.

ing_wild_boar.whatItIs: Game meat from wild pigs. Note: It is useful for elimination diets.
ing_wild_boar.whyItsHere: Included as a novel protein source for animals reacting to common meats.

ing_artificial_flavor.whatItIs: Flavour compounds produced synthetically rather than extracted from food.
ing_artificial_flavor.whyItsHere: Added to make the food more appealing to eat.

ing_blood_meal.whatItIs: Dried animal blood, one of the most protein-dense ingredients available. The label does not say which animal.
ing_blood_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts blood meal's allergen risk at medium, and the source animal is not named.

ing_dried_skim_milk.whatItIs: Milk with the fat removed, then spray dried to a powder.
ing_dried_skim_milk.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and for palatability.
ing_dried_skim_milk.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and puts its allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_shrimp_meal.whatItIs: Dried ground shrimp. Note: It contains chitin and natural glucosamine from the shells.
ing_shrimp_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source that also supplies natural glucosamine.
ing_shrimp_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_lactobacillus_acidophilus.whatItIs: A specific beneficial bacterium. Our data describes it as supporting the gut microbiome.
ing_lactobacillus_acidophilus.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic supporting digestion.

ing_duck_fat.whatItIs: Fat rendered from duck, an energy-dense ingredient that carries flavour.
ing_duck_fat.whyItsHere: Included as an energy source and to make the food more appealing.

ing_egg_yolk.whatItIs: The yellow part of the egg. Note: It is rich in vitamins A, D and E and in choline.
ing_egg_yolk.whyItsHere: Included for its fat, vitamins and lecithin.
ing_egg_yolk.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts egg yolk's allergen risk at medium.

ing_strawberries.whatItIs: A soft red fruit contributing antioxidants and fibre.
ing_strawberries.whyItsHere: Included as a source of antioxidants and fibre.
ing_strawberries.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation, noting they are high in sugar and should be used sparingly.

ing_hydrolyzed_soy.whatItIs: Soy protein broken into fragments small enough that the immune system is less likely to react.
ing_hydrolyzed_soy.whyItsHere: Included as a hypoallergenic plant protein for animals reacting to intact proteins.

ing_rice_hulls.whatItIs: The tough outer casing of the rice grain, a by-product of milling. It is almost entirely insoluble fibre.
ing_rice_hulls.whyItsHere: Included as an insoluble fibre source adding bulk.

ing_sodium_benzoate.whatItIs: A synthesised salt used to stop microbes growing.
ing_sodium_benzoate.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes some pets may be sensitive to sodium benzoate, and that it is generally considered safe in small amounts. It is rated caution.

ing_goose.whatItIs: Goose meat, commonly chosen as a novel protein.
ing_goose.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.

ing_artificial_colors.whatItIs: Synthetic dyes added to change how the food looks. They do nothing else.
ing_artificial_colors.whyItsHere: Added purely for appearance, which matters to the person buying rather than the animal eating.
ing_artificial_colors.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes artificial colours have no nutritional benefit, and mention potential behavioural effects. Our data suggests considering products with natural colourants. Rated caution.

ing_buckwheat.whatItIs: A pseudo-grain. Note: It is not related to wheat and is naturally gluten-free.
ing_buckwheat.whyItsHere: Included as a gluten-free carbohydrate source.

ing_anchovy.whatItIs: A small oily marine fish, naturally rich in omega-3.
ing_anchovy.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and as an omega-3 source.
ing_anchovy.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts anchovy's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_dried_brewers_yeast.whatItIs: Yeast from brewing, dried for use as an ingredient. It carries B vitamins and a savoury flavour.
ing_dried_brewers_yeast.whyItsHere: Included as a source of B vitamins and to improve flavour.

ing_dried_yogurt.whatItIs: Yogurt dried to a powder, keeping its protein and flavour in shelf-stable form.
ing_dried_yogurt.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and to make the food more appealing.
