ing_dried_yogurt.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_poultry_digest.whatItIs: Poultry tissue broken down with enzymes into a concentrated savoury liquid, sprayed onto kibble.
ing_poultry_digest.whyItsHere: Added purely to make the food taste better.
ing_poultry_digest.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and the label says poultry rather than naming the bird.

ing_whole_milk.whatItIs: Cow's milk with its fat intact, supplying protein, fat and calcium.
ing_whole_milk.whyItsHere: Included for its protein, fat and calcium.
ing_whole_milk.whatToWatchFor: Many adult pets are lactose intolerant. Rated safe in moderation, with an allergen risk of medium.

ing_clove_oil.whatItIs: An essential oil from clove. Note: It contains eugenol.
ing_clove_oil.whyItsHere: Included as an essential oil, typically for scent or flavour.
ing_clove_oil.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats and caution for dogs, and the safety guidance says eugenol can cause liver toxicity and to avoid topical application. Listed symptoms include liver toxicity, vomiting and tremors. Its allergen risk is high.

ing_cream.whatItIs: The fat-rich layer separated from milk. Our data describes it as a high fat dairy product.
ing_cream.whyItsHere: Included as a fat source and to make the food more appealing.
ing_cream.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and puts its allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_enterococcus_faecium.whatItIs: A specific beneficial bacterium. Our data describes it as a common pet food probiotic.
ing_enterococcus_faecium.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic supporting gut health.

ing_goat.whatItIs: Goat meat, commonly chosen as a novel protein an animal is unlikely to have eaten.
ing_goat.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.

ing_hydrolyzed_fish_protein.whatItIs: Fish protein broken down by enzymes into fragments the immune system is less likely to react to.
ing_hydrolyzed_fish_protein.whyItsHere: Included as a hypoallergenic protein, for pets with fish sensitivities per our data.

ing_hydrolyzed_poultry_protein.whatItIs: Poultry protein broken down by enzymes into fragments the immune system is less likely to react to.
ing_hydrolyzed_poultry_protein.whyItsHere: Included as a hypoallergenic protein, for pets with poultry sensitivities per our data.

ing_eucalyptus_oil.whatItIs: An essential oil distilled from eucalyptus leaves.
ing_eucalyptus_oil.whyItsHere: Included as an essential oil, typically for scent.
ing_eucalyptus_oil.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats and caution for dogs, flagged as a critical safety concern: it is toxic to both. Listed symptoms include salivation, vomiting, diarrhea, weakness and CNS depression. Note: Cats lack the enzymes to metabolise it. Allergen risk is high.

ing_l_leucine.whatItIs: A branched-chain amino acid added in synthesised form. Note: Its importance for muscle protein synthesis.
ing_l_leucine.whyItsHere: Added to balance the amino acid profile of the finished diet.

ing_dried_catnip.whatItIs: Dried catnip leaf. Our data lists it for cat products.
ing_dried_catnip.whyItsHere: Included as an attractant for enrichment rather than nutrition.

ing_chlorophyll.whatItIs: The green pigment extracted from plants. Note: It is also used for breath freshening.
ing_chlorophyll.whyItsHere: Added as a natural green colourant.

ing_krill_oil.whatItIs: Oil from krill, carrying both omega-3 fats and the red pigment astaxanthin.

ing_poultry_meal.whatItIs: Poultry rendered and dried into a concentrated protein. The label says poultry rather than naming the bird.
ing_poultry_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_poultry_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and which bird it came from is not stated.

ing_menadione.whatItIs: Vitamin K3, a synthetic form of vitamin K. Note: Natural K1 or K2 are preferred.
ing_menadione.whyItsHere: Included as a vitamin K supplement.
ing_menadione.whatToWatchFor: Our data and the safety guidance both raise safety concerns about this synthetic form and prefer natural vitamin K1 or K2. It is rated caution.

ing_annatto.whatItIs: A colourant from achiote seeds. Our data describes it as a natural alternative to synthetic dyes.
ing_annatto.whyItsHere: Added for yellow-orange colour, using a plant source rather than a synthetic dye.

ing_oranges.whatItIs: A citrus fruit, used without peel or seeds. Our data lists it for dog products.
ing_oranges.whyItsHere: Included as a source of vitamin C.
ing_oranges.whatToWatchFor: Remove the peel and seeds. Citrus oils can upset cats, and oranges are rated safe in moderation.

ing_bacon_flavor.whatItIs: A processed flavouring that gives the smoky, savoury taste of bacon.
ing_bacon_flavor.whyItsHere: Added to make the food more appealing to eat.
ing_bacon_flavor.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_pinto_beans.whatItIs: A speckled bean contributing plant protein and fibre.
ing_pinto_beans.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.
ing_pinto_beans.whatToWatchFor: Our data states pinto beans must be cooked thoroughly.

ing_black_beans.whatItIs: A small dark bean. Note: It is rich in antioxidants as well as protein and fibre.
ing_black_beans.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.
ing_black_beans.whatToWatchFor: Our data states black beans must be cooked.

ing_l_valine.whatItIs: A branched-chain amino acid, added in synthesised form alongside leucine and isoleucine.
ing_l_valine.whyItsHere: Added to balance the amino acid profile of the finished diet.

ing_l_phenylalanine.whatItIs: An essential amino acid added in synthesised form. Note: It is a precursor to tyrosine.
ing_l_phenylalanine.whyItsHere: Added to balance the amino acid profile of the finished diet.

ing_l_isoleucine.whatItIs: One of the three branched-chain amino acids, added in synthesised form.
ing_l_isoleucine.whyItsHere: Added to balance the amino acid profile of the finished diet.

ing_l_histidine.whatItIs: An essential amino acid added in synthesised form. Note: It is a precursor to histamine.
ing_l_histidine.whyItsHere: Added to balance the amino acid profile of the finished diet.

ing_bromelain.whatItIs: An enzyme extracted from pineapple that breaks down protein. Note: It also has anti-inflammatory properties.
ing_bromelain.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive enzyme helping break down protein.

ing_lobster.whatItIs: A shellfish used as a premium protein. Our data flags it as a potential allergen.
ing_lobster.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and because animals find it appealing.
ing_lobster.whatToWatchFor: Note: Lobster is shellfish and a potential allergen, putting its allergen risk at medium.

ing_bifidobacterium_animalis.whatItIs: A specific beneficial bacterium. Our data describes it as a species-specific probiotic strain.
ing_bifidobacterium_animalis.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic supporting intestinal health.

ing_malic_acid.whatItIs: An acid found naturally in apples, used to adjust sourness and pH.
ing_malic_acid.whyItsHere: Added as an acidifier and to enhance flavour.

ing_soy_protein.whatItIs: Protein from soybeans. Our data describes it as a common allergen in some pets.
ing_soy_protein.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein source.
ing_soy_protein.whatToWatchFor: Our data describes soy protein as a common allergen in some pets and puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_parabens.whatItIs: A family of synthetic preservatives. Note: Many brands avoid them.
ing_parabens.whyItsHere: Added as a preservative to extend shelf life.
ing_parabens.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution. Many brands avoid them, and the allergen risk is low to medium.

ing_msg.whatItIs: Monosodium glutamate, a synthesised flavour enhancer.
ing_msg.whyItsHere: Added to intensify the savoury taste of the food.
ing_msg.whatToWatchFor: Rated MSG as caution and notes some pets may be sensitive to it.

ing_cantaloupe.whatItIs: A melon, used without rind or seeds. It is mostly water and carries vitamins.
ing_cantaloupe.whyItsHere: Included for its vitamins and moisture.
ing_cantaloupe.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to remove the rind and seeds.

ing_seaweed.whatItIs: Marine algae, dried for use as an ingredient. Note: It is a natural source of iodine and trace minerals.
ing_seaweed.whyItsHere: Included as a mineral source, particularly iodine.

ing_mussel.whatItIs: A shellfish. Note: Green-lipped mussels provide glucosamine.
ing_mussel.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and for joint support.
ing_mussel.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts mussel's allergen risk at low to medium. It is shellfish.

ing_liver_digest.whatItIs: Liver broken down with enzymes into a concentrated savoury liquid. Our data describes it as highly palatable.
ing_liver_digest.whyItsHere: Added to make the food taste better; it is sprayed onto kibble.

ing_valerian_root.whatItIs: A dried root. Our data describes it as an alternative to catnip that some cats prefer. Our data lists it for cat products.
ing_valerian_root.whyItsHere: Included as an attractant and for its calming association.

ing_butter.whatItIs: Churned cream. Note: It is very low in lactose.
ing_butter.whyItsHere: Included as a fat source in the recipe.
ing_butter.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and puts its allergen risk at low to medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_papain.whatItIs: An enzyme extracted from papaya fruit that breaks down protein.
ing_papain.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive enzyme helping break down protein.

ing_methylcellulose.whatItIs: A modified plant fibre. Note: Its FDA GRAS status and that it is non-digestible.
ing_methylcellulose.whyItsHere: Added to thicken and bind the food; it also acts as fibre.

ing_cauliflower.whatItIs: A cruciferous vegetable contributing fibre and vitamins.
ing_cauliflower.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and vitamins.
ing_cauliflower.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and notes it can cause gas.

ing_cellulose_gum.whatItIs: Carboxymethyl cellulose, made from plant cellulose. Note: Its FDA GRAS status.
ing_cellulose_gum.whyItsHere: Added to thicken the food and keep it stable.

ing_beef_by_products.whatItIs: Parts of the cow other than muscle meat. Our data says this includes organs and tissues.
ing_beef_by_products.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source; organ tissue is nutrient-dense.
ing_beef_by_products.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts the allergen risk at medium, and the exact mix of parts is not stated on the label.

ing_tea_tree_oil.whatItIs: An essential oil from the melaleuca tree.
ing_tea_tree_oil.whyItsHere: Included as an essential oil, typically in topical products.
ing_tea_tree_oil.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: it can be toxic even at low concentrations, especially if licked off the coat. Listed symptoms include weakness, incoordination, tremors and hypothermia. Allergen risk is high.

ing_squid.whatItIs: A cephalopod used as a lean seafood protein. Note: It is high in taurine for cats.
ing_squid.whyItsHere: Included as a lean protein source that also supplies taurine.

ing_sorghum_flour.whatItIs: Ground sorghum, a naturally gluten-free grain.
ing_sorghum_flour.whyItsHere: Included as a gluten-free carbohydrate source.

ing_lactobacillus_casei.whatItIs: A lactobacillus species widely used in fermented dairy, cultured and dried for food use.
ing_lactobacillus_casei.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic, associated in our data with immune support.

ing_grape_seed_extract.whatItIs: An extract of grape seeds. Note: The seed extract is safe unlike grape fruit or flesh, and is rich in proanthocyanidins.

ing_ethoxyquin.whatItIs: A synthetic antioxidant preservative. Note: The FDA has restricted its use and that it is banned in some countries.
ing_ethoxyquin.whyItsHere: Added as a preservative to stop fats going rancid.
ing_ethoxyquin.whatToWatchFor: Our data and the safety guidance both describe ethoxyquin as controversial, associate it with liver and kidney concerns, and note many owners prefer foods without it. It is rated caution.

ing_fragrance.whatItIs: A synthetic scent additive. Our data states a preference for fragrance-free products.
ing_fragrance.whyItsHere: Added for scent, which is for the owner rather than the animal.
ing_fragrance.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution, prefers fragrance-free, and puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_spirulina.whatItIs: A blue-green algae, dried and powdered for use as an ingredient.
ing_spirulina.whyItsHere: Included as an antioxidant source, associated in our data with immune support.

ing_bacillus_coagulans.whatItIs: A spore-forming probiotic bacterium. Note: It is heat-stable and survives processing.
ing_bacillus_coagulans.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic that stays viable through manufacturing.

ing_bifidobacterium_bifidum.whatItIs: A bifidobacterium species, one of the groups that dominate a healthy large intestine.
ing_bifidobacterium_bifidum.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic supporting digestion.

ing_meat_meal.whatItIs: Mammal tissue rendered and dried into a concentrated protein. The label does not say which animal.
ing_meat_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_meat_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and neither the animal nor the tissues are named.

ing_wheat_germ.whatItIs: The nutrient-rich embryo of the wheat kernel, separated during milling.
ing_wheat_germ.whyItsHere: Included as a source of vitamin E and B vitamins.
ing_wheat_germ.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts wheat germ's allergen risk at medium.

ing_lactose.whatItIs: Milk sugar, extracted from milk. Note: Many pets are lactose intolerant.
ing_lactose.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate and to sweeten the product.
ing_lactose.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution. Many pets are lactose intolerant, and the allergen risk is medium to high.

ing_anchovy_oil.whatItIs: Oil from anchovies. Note: It is high in EPA and DHA and a sustainable source.

ing_kidney_beans.whatItIs: A red bean contributing plant protein and fibre.
ing_kidney_beans.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.
ing_kidney_beans.whatToWatchFor: Our data states kidney beans must be fully cooked, because raw ones contain lectins.

ing_lycopene.whatItIs: The red pigment extracted from tomatoes, which also acts as an antioxidant.
ing_lycopene.whyItsHere: Added for red colour, and it contributes antioxidants.

ing_hydrolyzed_salmon.whatItIs: Salmon protein broken down into fragments the immune system is less likely to react to. Note: Its use in prescription diets.
ing_hydrolyzed_salmon.whyItsHere: Included as a hypoallergenic protein source.

ing_pheasant.whatItIs: A game bird with darker meat than chicken, commonly chosen as a novel protein.
ing_pheasant.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.

ing_dried_goat_milk.whatItIs: Goat milk dried to a powder, keeping its protein in shelf-stable form.
ing_dried_goat_milk.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, chosen for its digestibility.
ing_dried_goat_milk.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium. It is still a dairy ingredient.

ing_elk.whatItIs: Elk meat, a lean game meat. Note: It is useful for elimination diets.
ing_elk.whyItsHere: Included as a novel protein source for animals reacting to common meats.

ing_beet_juice_color.whatItIs: Juice from beets, used as a natural colourant.
ing_beet_juice_color.whyItsHere: Added for red-pink colour, using a vegetable rather than a synthetic dye.

ing_shea_butter.whatItIs: Fat from the shea nut, used on skin rather than in food.
ing_shea_butter.whyItsHere: Included in topical products as a balm for paws and nose.

ing_amylase.whatItIs: An enzyme that breaks starch into simpler sugars. Note: It aids carbohydrate digestion.
ing_amylase.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive enzyme helping break down starch.

ing_cellulase.whatItIs: An enzyme that breaks down plant fibre. Note: It aids fibre breakdown.
ing_cellulase.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive enzyme helping break down plant fibre.

ing_lipase.whatItIs: An enzyme that breaks down fat. Note: It aids fat digestion.
ing_lipase.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive enzyme helping break down fat.

ing_cocamidopropyl_betaine.whatItIs: A synthesised surfactant used in shampoos to lift dirt and oil.
ing_cocamidopropyl_betaine.whyItsHere: Included in topical products as the cleansing agent.
ing_cocamidopropyl_betaine.whatToWatchFor: It can irritate very sensitive skin. Rated safe for most rather than simply safe, with an allergen risk of medium.

ing_phenoxyethanol.whatItIs: A synthesised preservative used in topical products.
ing_phenoxyethanol.whyItsHere: Added to stop microbes growing in the product.
ing_phenoxyethanol.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution. It can irritate some pets, and the allergen risk is low to medium.

ing_nutmeg.whatItIs: A spice ground from the nutmeg seed. Note: It contains myristicin.
ing_nutmeg.whyItsHere: Included as a spice for flavour.
ing_nutmeg.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats. The safety guidance says myristicin causes hallucinations, increased heart rate, disorientation and seizures.

ing_bacillus_subtilis.whatItIs: A spore-forming probiotic bacterium. Note: It survives food processing.
ing_bacillus_subtilis.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic that stays viable through manufacturing.

ing_aloe_vera.whatItIs: Gel from the aloe leaf, used on skin as a soothing botanical.
ing_aloe_vera.whyItsHere: Included in topical products for its soothing properties.

ing_skim_milk.whatItIs: Cow's milk with the fat separated off. Note: The lactose is still present.
ing_skim_milk.whyItsHere: Included as a protein and calcium source.
ing_skim_milk.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation. The lactose is still present, and the allergen risk is medium.

ing_dried_ginger.whatItIs: Dehydrated ginger root, associated in our data with digestion.
ing_dried_ginger.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive aid in dried form.
ing_dried_ginger.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation rather than simply safe.

ing_dried_fermentation_products.whatItIs: Dried residues of fermentation. Note: They contain beneficial enzymes and metabolites.
ing_dried_fermentation_products.whyItsHere: Included as a source of enzymes and probiotic metabolites.

ing_millet_flour.whatItIs: Ground millet, a naturally gluten-free grain.
ing_millet_flour.whyItsHere: Included as a gluten-free carbohydrate source.

ing_cricket_protein.whatItIs: Protein from farmed crickets. Note: It is sustainable and has a complete amino acid profile.
ing_cricket_protein.whyItsHere: Included as an alternative protein source with a lower environmental cost.

ing_bone_meal.whatItIs: Ground bone, supplying calcium and phosphorus in the ratio they occur in bone.
ing_bone_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a calcium and phosphorus source.

ing_whey_protein_isolate.whatItIs: Whey processed to isolate the protein. Note: Most lactose is removed.
ing_whey_protein_isolate.whyItsHere: Included as a highly concentrated protein source.
ing_whey_protein_isolate.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium. It is still a dairy-derived ingredient.

ing_ostrich.whatItIs: Ostrich meat, a lean poultry alternative. Note: It is useful for elimination diets.
ing_ostrich.whyItsHere: Included as a novel protein source for animals reacting to common meats.

ing_acetic_acid.whatItIs: The acid that makes vinegar sour, produced by fermentation.
ing_acetic_acid.whyItsHere: Added as an acidifier and preservative.

ing_plums.whatItIs: A smooth-skinned stone fruit, used without the pit. It contributes vitamins and fibre.
ing_plums.whyItsHere: Included as a source of vitamins and fibre.
ing_plums.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to remove the pit.

ing_vitamin_e_supplement.whatItIs: A synthesised form of vitamin E. Note: It protects cell membranes.
ing_vitamin_e_supplement.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient and antioxidant.

ing_acacia_gum.whatItIs: Hardened sap from the acacia tree. Note: It is the same as gum arabic.
ing_acacia_gum.whyItsHere: Added as a stabiliser; it also acts as prebiotic fibre.

ing_acai.whatItIs: A palm berry. Note: It is high in anthocyanins and has antioxidant properties.

ing_acorn_squash.whatItIs: A winter squash, cooked before use, contributing carbohydrate and fibre.
ing_acorn_squash.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate and fibre source.

ing_adzuki_beans.whatItIs: A small red bean contributing plant protein and fibre.
ing_adzuki_beans.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.

ing_alcohol.whatItIs: Ethanol, used as a solvent rather than as an ingredient in its own right.
ing_alcohol.whyItsHere: Present as a solvent, typically carrying other ingredients.
ing_alcohol.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: it can be fatal, and pets are much more sensitive than humans. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, incoordination, CNS depression, difficulty breathing, tremors and coma.

ing_alligator.whatItIs: Alligator meat, a rare protein. Note: It is useful for severe food allergies.
ing_alligator.whyItsHere: Included as an exotic novel protein for animals reacting to everything more common.

ing_amaranth.whatItIs: A gluten-free pseudo-grain. Note: It is high in protein and lysine.
ing_amaranth.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source that also contributes protein.

ing_anchovy_meal.whatItIs: Anchovies rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_anchovy_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated fish protein source.
ing_anchovy_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_animal_fat.whatItIs: Rendered fat. Our data describes the source as unspecified, so the label does not say which animal it came from.
ing_animal_fat.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated energy source.
ing_animal_fat.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and because the animal is unspecified you cannot tell what it is.

ing_arrowroot.whatItIs: Starch from the arrowroot tuber. Our data describes it as a grain-free thickener that is gentle on digestion.
ing_arrowroot.whyItsHere: Included as an easily digestible starch and thickener.

ing_ascorbic_acid_preservative.whatItIs: Vitamin C used for its antioxidant effect rather than as a nutrient.
ing_ascorbic_acid_preservative.whyItsHere: Added as a preservative, slowing fats from going rancid.

ing_aspergillus_oryzae.whatItIs: A fermentation extract from a food-grade mould. Note: It is a source of amylase and protease enzymes.
ing_aspergillus_oryzae.whyItsHere: Included as an enzyme source aiding digestion.

ing_bakers_chocolate.whatItIs: Unsweetened baking chocolate. Note: It has the highest theobromine concentration of any chocolate.
ing_bakers_chocolate.whyItsHere: Present as a baking ingredient in the product.
ing_bakers_chocolate.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats and describes it as the most dangerous form of chocolate for pets. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, hyperactivity, abnormal heart rhythm, tremors, seizures and death.

ing_barley_flour.whatItIs: Ground barley, used as a carbohydrate source.
ing_barley_flour.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source in the recipe.

ing_beef_digest.whatItIs: Beef tissue broken down with enzymes into a concentrated savoury liquid.
ing_beef_digest.whyItsHere: Added to make the food taste better; it is sprayed onto kibble.
ing_beef_digest.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_beef_fat.whatItIs: Fat rendered from cattle, an energy-dense ingredient that carries flavour.
ing_beef_fat.whyItsHere: Included as an energy source and to make the food more appealing.
ing_beef_fat.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts beef fat's allergen risk at medium.

ing_beef_fresh.whatItIs: Fresh meat from cattle, used as the main protein in the recipe.
ing_beef_fresh.whyItsHere: Included as the primary protein source for the diet.
ing_beef_fresh.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium for dogs and high for cats.

ing_beef_heart.whatItIs: Cardiac muscle from cattle. Note: It is a natural source of taurine and CoQ10.
ing_beef_heart.whyItsHere: Included as an organ meat, particularly for its taurine.
ing_beef_heart.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_beef_kidney.whatItIs: Kidney from cattle. Note: It is rich in B12 and selenium.
ing_beef_kidney.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense organ meat.
ing_beef_kidney.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_beef_liver.whatItIs: Liver from cattle. Note: It is rich in vitamin A, iron and B vitamins.
ing_beef_liver.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense organ meat and for palatability.
ing_beef_liver.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts beef liver's allergen risk at medium.

ing_beef_lung.whatItIs: Lung tissue from cattle. Our data describes it as a low fat, high protein organ meat.
ing_beef_lung.whyItsHere: Included as an organ meat contributing lean protein.

ing_beef_meal.whatItIs: Beef rendered and dried, leaving a much more concentrated protein than fresh meat.
ing_beef_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_beef_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium for dogs and high for cats.

ing_beef_tripe.whatItIs: Stomach lining from cattle. Note: Green tripe contains beneficial enzymes and probiotics.
ing_beef_tripe.whyItsHere: Included as an organ meat and for its digestive enzymes.

ing_bell_pepper.whatItIs: A sweet pepper, used without seeds or stem. It is a notably rich source of vitamin C.
ing_bell_pepper.whyItsHere: Included for its vitamin C and antioxidants.
ing_bell_pepper.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to remove the seeds and stem.

ing_benzoyl_peroxide.whatItIs: A synthesised medicated cleansing agent used on skin.
ing_benzoyl_peroxide.whyItsHere: Included in medicated topical products as the active cleanser.
ing_benzoyl_peroxide.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution. It can be drying, and the allergen risk is medium.

ing_beta_glucanase.whatItIs: An enzyme that breaks down beta-glucan fibre.
ing_beta_glucanase.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive enzyme helping break down that fibre.

ing_bifidobacterium_longum.whatItIs: A bifidobacterium species commonly used in supplements, cultured and dried for food use.
ing_bifidobacterium_longum.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic, associated in our data with immune support.

ing_bison_meal.whatItIs: Bison rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_bison_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated novel-protein source.

ing_black_soldier_fly.whatItIs: Larvae of the black soldier fly. Note: They are AAFCO approved and high in lauric acid.
ing_black_soldier_fly.whyItsHere: Included as a sustainable insect protein with a lower environmental cost.

ing_brussels_sprouts.whatItIs: A small cruciferous vegetable. Our data lists it for dog products.
ing_brussels_sprouts.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and vitamins.
ing_brussels_sprouts.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and notes they can cause significant gas.

ing_buttermilk.whatItIs: The liquid left over from churning butter, described in our data as a by-product of butter making.
ing_buttermilk.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and naturally occurring probiotics.
ing_buttermilk.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and puts its allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_caffeine.whatItIs: A natural stimulant found in coffee, tea and cocoa.
ing_caffeine.whyItsHere: Present as a stimulant compound, generally carried in by another ingredient.
ing_caffeine.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, flagged as a critical safety concern, noting there is no antidote. Listed symptoms include restlessness, rapid breathing, heart palpitations, muscle tremors, seizures and hyperactivity.

ing_calcium_carbonate.whatItIs: A mineral calcium salt. Our data describes it as the most common calcium supplement.
ing_calcium_carbonate.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its calcium requirement.

ing_calcium_iodate.whatItIs: A synthesised calcium salt of iodine, the form most often used to fortify pet food.
ing_calcium_iodate.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts so the diet meets its iodine requirement.

ing_carbon_black.whatItIs: A black pigment made from charred vegetable matter.

ing_carboxymethylcellulose.whatItIs: Chemically modified cellulose. Note: It is common in wet foods.
ing_carboxymethylcellulose.whyItsHere: Added to thicken the food and keep it stable.

ing_chicken_by_product_meal.whatItIs: Chicken by-products rendered and dried into a concentrated protein — organ and other non-muscle tissue rather than breast meat.
ing_chicken_by_product_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_chicken_by_product_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and which parts went into it is not stated on the label.

ing_chicken_digest.whatItIs: Chicken tissue broken down with enzymes into a concentrated savoury liquid.
ing_chicken_digest.whyItsHere: Added to make the food taste better; it is sprayed onto kibble.
ing_chicken_digest.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_chicken_fresh.whatItIs: Fresh poultry meat, used as the main protein in the recipe.
ing_chicken_fresh.whyItsHere: Included as the primary protein source for the diet.
ing_chicken_fresh.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium for dogs and high for cats.

ing_chicken_heart.whatItIs: Cardiac muscle from chicken. Our data describes it as an excellent natural taurine source.
ing_chicken_heart.whyItsHere: Included as an organ meat, particularly for its taurine.
ing_chicken_heart.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_chicken_liver.whatItIs: Liver from chicken. Note: It is rich in vitamin A and iron.
ing_chicken_liver.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense organ meat and for palatability.
ing_chicken_liver.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_chicory_root.whatItIs: The root of the chicory plant, a natural source of inulin.
ing_chicory_root.whyItsHere: Included as a prebiotic fibre feeding the gut's own bacteria.

ing_chives.whatItIs: A herb in the allium family, the same group as onion and garlic.
ing_chives.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats and caution for dogs. The safety guidance says they can cause gastrointestinal upset and red blood cell damage. Listed symptoms include gastrointestinal irritation, anemia, weakness, pale gums and elevated heart rate.

ing_chlorella.whatItIs: A green freshwater algae, dried and powdered.
ing_chlorella.whyItsHere: Included as a source of chlorophyll, associated in our data with detoxification.

ing_chlorhexidine.whatItIs: A synthesised antiseptic used in medicated topical products.
ing_chlorhexidine.whyItsHere: Included in medicated cleansers as the active agent.

ing_chocolate.whatItIs: A confection made from cocoa. Note: It contains theobromine and that dark chocolate is most dangerous.
ing_chocolate.whyItsHere: Present as a flavouring in the product.
ing_chocolate.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, flagged as a critical safety concern — they say to contact your vet immediately if it is eaten. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, excessive thirst, restlessness, tremors, seizures and abnormal heart rhythm.

ing_choline_chloride.whatItIs: The usual added form of choline. Note: It is often grouped with the B vitamins.
ing_choline_chloride.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, associated with liver and brain function.

ing_chromium.whatItIs: A trace mineral. Our data associates it with glucose metabolism and insulin function.
ing_chromium.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts as a supplementary mineral.

ing_citrus_oil.whatItIs: An essential oil from citrus peel. Note: It contains limonene and linalool.
ing_citrus_oil.whyItsHere: Included as an essential oil, typically for scent.
ing_citrus_oil.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: cats cannot metabolise limonene and linalool, and it can cause liver damage and CNS depression. Allergen risk is high.

ing_clam.whatItIs: A shellfish used for its protein and its strong savoury flavour.
ing_clam.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and to make the food more appealing.
ing_clam.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts clam's allergen risk at low to medium. It is shellfish.

ing_cobalt_sulfate.whatItIs: A synthesised cobalt salt. Note: Cobalt is essential for vitamin B12.
ing_cobalt_sulfate.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts as a cobalt source.

ing_coco_glucoside.whatItIs: A mild surfactant derived from coconut. Note: It is sulfate free.
ing_coco_glucoside.whyItsHere: Included in topical products as a gentle cleansing agent.

ing_cocoa.whatItIs: Processed cocoa bean. Note: It contains theobromine.
ing_cocoa.whyItsHere: Present as a flavouring in the product.
ing_cocoa.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, and the safety guidance says cocoa powder is extremely concentrated. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, excessive thirst, restlessness, tremors, seizures and abnormal heart rhythm.

ing_cocoa_bean_hulls.whatItIs: A by-product of cocoa processing, used as garden mulch rather than as food. Note: Dogs are attracted to the smell.
ing_cocoa_bean_hulls.whyItsHere: Present as garden mulch — our data states it is not for food use.
ing_cocoa_bean_hulls.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats because of their theobromine content. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, hyperactivity, tremors and seizures.

ing_cocoa_powder.whatItIs: Dried and processed cocoa. Note: It has a very high theobromine concentration and is one of the most toxic forms for pets.
ing_cocoa_powder.whyItsHere: Present as a flavouring or baking ingredient.
ing_cocoa_powder.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, hyperactivity, abnormal heart rhythm, tremors, seizures and death.

ing_cod_meal.whatItIs: Cod rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_cod_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated fish protein source.
ing_cod_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_coffee.whatItIs: Roasted and ground coffee. Note: It contains caffeine.
ing_coffee.whyItsHere: Present as a flavouring in the product.
ing_coffee.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, and the safety guidance says grounds and beans are especially dangerous because the caffeine is concentrated. Listed symptoms include hyperactivity, restlessness, vomiting, elevated heart rate, seizures and tremors.

ing_coffee_beans.whatItIs: Roasted coffee beans. Note: Whole beans and grounds are more dangerous than brewed coffee because the caffeine is concentrated.
ing_coffee_beans.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats. Listed symptoms include hyperactivity, restlessness, vomiting, elevated heart rate, seizures, tremors and death.

ing_colloidal_oatmeal.whatItIs: Finely milled oats that suspend in water, used on skin rather than in food.
ing_colloidal_oatmeal.whyItsHere: Included in topical products as a skin protectant.

ing_copper_chlorophyllin.whatItIs: A modified form of chlorophyll. Note: It is more stable than the natural pigment.
ing_copper_chlorophyllin.whyItsHere: Added for green colour; our data also associates it with breath freshening.

ing_copper_sulfate.whatItIs: A synthesised copper salt, the common inorganic copper supplement.
ing_copper_sulfate.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts so the diet meets its copper requirement.

ing_corn_bran.whatItIs: The outer layer of the corn kernel. Our data describes it as insoluble fibre.
ing_corn_bran.whyItsHere: Included as an insoluble fibre source adding bulk.

ing_corn_meal.whatItIs: Ground corn, used as a carbohydrate source.
ing_corn_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source in the recipe.
ing_corn_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts corn meal's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_cornstarch.whatItIs: Pure starch extracted from corn, with the protein and fibre removed.
ing_cornstarch.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and to thicken the food.

ing_crab_meal.whatItIs: Crab dried and ground. Note: It contains shell material, which is where its calcium comes from.
ing_crab_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a protein and calcium source.
ing_crab_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts crab meal's allergen risk at medium. It is shellfish and contains shell material.

ing_cucumber.whatItIs: A watery vegetable, very low in calories.
ing_cucumber.whyItsHere: Included as a low-calorie ingredient contributing moisture.

ing_currants.whatItIs: Small dried fruit, related to grapes despite the name.
ing_currants.whyItsHere: Present as a dried fruit in the product.
ing_currants.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for dogs and caution for cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: they carry the same risk as grapes and raisins and can cause acute kidney failure. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy, anorexia, abdominal pain and kidney failure.

ing_dark_chocolate.whatItIs: Chocolate with a high cacao content. Note: It has more theobromine than milk chocolate.
ing_dark_chocolate.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats and notes it is more toxic than milk chocolate. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, hyperactivity, abnormal heart rhythm, tremors and seizures.

ing_decyl_glucoside.whatItIs: A mild plant-derived surfactant. Note: It is sulfate free.
ing_decyl_glucoside.whyItsHere: Included in topical products as a gentle cleansing agent.

ing_dmdm_hydantoin.whatItIs: A synthesised preservative. Our data describes it as formaldehyde releasing.
ing_dmdm_hydantoin.whyItsHere: Added as a preservative in topical products.
ing_dmdm_hydantoin.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution and described as formaldehyde releasing, with an allergen risk of medium.

ing_dried_apples.whatItIs: Dehydrated apple, contributing fibre and a sweet flavour.
ing_dried_apples.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source that also improves palatability.

ing_dried_beet_pulp.whatItIs: Dried fibre left after sugar extraction from beets.
ing_dried_beet_pulp.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source in the recipe.

ing_dried_blueberries.whatItIs: Dehydrated blueberries, included for their antioxidant content.
ing_dried_blueberries.whyItsHere: Included as a source of antioxidants.

ing_dried_buttermilk.whatItIs: Buttermilk spray dried to a shelf-stable powder.
ing_dried_buttermilk.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and for palatability.
ing_dried_buttermilk.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and puts its allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_dried_carrots.whatItIs: Dehydrated carrot, contributing beta carotene and fibre.
ing_dried_carrots.whyItsHere: Included as a source of beta carotene and fibre.

ing_dried_casein.whatItIs: The main protein in milk, separated out and dried to a powder.
ing_dried_casein.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source in the recipe.
ing_dried_casein.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts dried casein's allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_dried_cranberries.whatItIs: Dehydrated cranberries, associated in our data with urinary tract health.
ing_dried_cranberries.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to avoid sweetened varieties.

ing_dried_egg.whatItIs: Whole egg dried to a powder, giving a concentrated protein that also binds.
ing_dried_egg.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source and as a binder.
ing_dried_egg.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts dried egg's allergen risk at medium.

ing_dried_egg_yolk.whatItIs: Egg yolk spray dried to a powder, concentrating its fat and vitamins.
ing_dried_egg_yolk.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated source of fat and vitamins.
ing_dried_egg_yolk.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_dried_fermentation_product.whatItIs: A generic dried fermentation product, described in our data without naming the organism.
ing_dried_fermentation_product.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic blend supporting digestion.

ing_dried_kelp.whatItIs: Dehydrated seaweed, a concentrated natural source of iodine and trace minerals.
ing_dried_kelp.whyItsHere: Included as a mineral source, particularly iodine.

ing_dried_milk.whatItIs: Milk spray dried to a powder, supplying protein and calcium.
ing_dried_milk.whyItsHere: Included as a protein and calcium source.
ing_dried_milk.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and puts its allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_dried_parsley.whatItIs: Dehydrated parsley, associated with freshening breath. Our data lists it for dog products.
ing_dried_parsley.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation rather than simply safe.

ing_dried_pumpkin.whatItIs: Dehydrated pumpkin, a concentrated source of soluble fibre.
ing_dried_pumpkin.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source supporting digestion.

ing_dried_spinach.whatItIs: Dehydrated spinach, contributing vitamins and minerals.
ing_dried_spinach.whyItsHere: Included as a source of vitamins and minerals.
ing_dried_spinach.whatToWatchFor: Note: Dried spinach is high in oxalates and rates it safe in moderation.

ing_duck_egg.whatItIs: Eggs from duck. Note: They are an alternative egg source, larger than chicken eggs.
ing_duck_egg.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense protein and as a less common egg option.

ing_duck_meal.whatItIs: Duck rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_duck_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated novel-protein source.

ing_edamame.whatItIs: Young soybeans, harvested before they harden.
ing_edamame.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein source.
ing_edamame.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts edamame's allergen risk at medium. It is soy.

ing_egg_product.whatItIs: A mixture of egg components rather than whole eggs.
ing_egg_product.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source and as a binder.
ing_egg_product.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and which parts of the egg are included is not stated.

ing_eggshell_calcium.whatItIs: Ground eggshell, a natural calcium source.
ing_eggshell_calcium.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its calcium requirement, using a food source rather than a mineral salt.

ing_fish_digest.whatItIs: Fish tissue broken down with enzymes into a concentrated savoury liquid.
ing_fish_digest.whyItsHere: Added to make the food taste better; it is sprayed onto kibble.
ing_fish_digest.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and the fish species is not named.

ing_fish_meal.whatItIs: A generic rendered fish product. The label does not say which species went into it.
ing_fish_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_fish_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium, and the species is not identified.

ing_fructooligosaccharides.whatItIs: Short chains of fruit sugars the animal does not digest. Note: They feed beneficial bacteria.
ing_fructooligosaccharides.whyItsHere: Included as a prebiotic fibre feeding the gut's own bacteria.

ing_goji_berries.whatItIs: A dried red berry. Note: It is rich in vitamins and antioxidants.

ing_grapes.whatItIs: A fruit. Note: The toxic compound is unknown but the effect is well documented.
ing_grapes.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for dogs and caution for cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: even small amounts are dangerous and they can cause acute kidney failure. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy, anorexia, abdominal pain, decreased urination and kidney failure.

ing_green_lentils.whatItIs: A pulse contributing plant protein and fibre.
ing_green_lentils.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.

ing_green_peas.whatItIs: Whole green peas, contributing protein, fibre and vitamins.
ing_green_peas.whyItsHere: Included as a source of plant protein, fibre and vitamins.

ing_ground_flaxseed.whatItIs: Flaxseed ground rather than left whole. Note: Ground seed is better absorbed.
ing_ground_flaxseed.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source and plant omega-3 source.

ing_guinea_fowl.whatItIs: A speckled game bird, leaner than chicken and commonly chosen as a novel protein.
ing_guinea_fowl.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.

ing_haddock.whatItIs: A lean white marine fish used as a protein source.
ing_haddock.whyItsHere: Included as a lean protein source.
ing_haddock.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts haddock's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_hemp_seeds.whatItIs: Seeds from the hemp plant. Note: Food-grade hemp contains no THC and supplies omega-3 and omega-6.
ing_hemp_seeds.whyItsHere: Included as a source of omega fatty acids and protein.

ing_herring_meal.whatItIs: Herring rendered and dried into a concentrated protein that also supplies omega-3.
ing_herring_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein and omega-3 source.
ing_herring_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_hops.whatItIs: The dried flower of the hop plant, used in brewing.
ing_hops.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: they cause malignant hyperthermia, with body temperature rising to potentially fatal levels. Both fresh and spent hops are dangerous. Listed symptoms include panting, high body temperature, seizures and death.

ing_hydrolyzed_meat_protein.whatItIs: Meat protein broken down by enzymes into fragments the immune system is less likely to react to.
ing_hydrolyzed_meat_protein.whyItsHere: Included as a hypoallergenic protein for pets with allergies.

ing_hydrolyzed_protein.whatItIs: Protein broken down into smaller fragments to reduce how strongly the immune system reacts to it.
ing_hydrolyzed_protein.whyItsHere: Included as a hypoallergenic protein source.

ing_hydrolyzed_vegetable_protein.whatItIs: Plant protein broken down by enzymes. Note: It adds umami flavour.
ing_hydrolyzed_vegetable_protein.whyItsHere: Included both as a protein source and to make the food taste better.

ing_iron_oxide_black.whatItIs: A naturally occurring mineral pigment giving black colour.
ing_iron_oxide_black.whyItsHere: Added purely for black colour, using a mineral rather than a synthetic dye.

ing_iron_oxide_red.whatItIs: A naturally occurring mineral pigment giving red-brown colour.
ing_iron_oxide_red.whyItsHere: Added purely for colour, using a mineral rather than a synthetic dye.

ing_iron_oxide_yellow.whatItIs: A naturally occurring mineral pigment giving yellow colour.
ing_iron_oxide_yellow.whyItsHere: Added purely for colour, using a mineral rather than a synthetic dye.

ing_iron_sulfate.whatItIs: Ferrous sulfate, the common inorganic iron supplement.
ing_iron_sulfate.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its iron requirement, supporting red blood cell production.

ing_kefir.whatItIs: Fermented milk. Note: It carries both beneficial bacteria and yeasts.
ing_kefir.whyItsHere: Included for its probiotics and protein.
ing_kefir.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts kefir's allergen risk at low to medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_konjac.whatItIs: Glucomannan extracted from the konjac root, a very absorbent soluble fibre.
ing_konjac.whyItsHere: Added to thicken the food; it also acts as fibre.

ing_krill.whatItIs: A small marine crustacean. Note: It is rich in phospholipid omega-3s.
ing_krill.whyItsHere: Included as an omega-3 source that also carries astaxanthin.

ing_l_glutamine.whatItIs: An amino acid added in synthesised form. Our data associates it with intestinal barrier function.
ing_l_glutamine.whyItsHere: Added as a supplementary amino acid, associated with gut health.

ing_lactobacillus_rhamnosus.whatItIs: A lactobacillus species known for sticking well to the gut lining, cultured and dried.
ing_lactobacillus_rhamnosus.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic supporting digestion.

ing_lamb_fresh.whatItIs: Fresh meat from sheep, often chosen as a novel protein.
ing_lamb_fresh.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source, and specifically as a novel-protein option.
ing_lamb_fresh.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts lamb's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_lamb_meal.whatItIs: Lamb rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_lamb_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_lamb_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_lard.whatItIs: Rendered and purified pork fat, an energy-dense ingredient.
ing_lard.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated energy source.
ing_lard.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts lard's allergen risk at medium. It is a pork product.

ing_leeks.whatItIs: A vegetable in the allium family, the same group as onion and garlic.
ing_leeks.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats and caution for dogs. The safety guidance says they can cause gastrointestinal upset and hemolytic anemia in quantity. Listed symptoms include gastrointestinal irritation, anemia, weakness and pale gums.

ing_lily.whatItIs: An ornamental flowering plant. Our data states it is not for food use.
ing_lily.whyItsHere: Present as an ornamental plant rather than a food ingredient.
ing_lily.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats: all parts are extremely toxic to them and cause acute kidney failure, and even pollen can be fatal. Our data records lilies as not known to be toxic to dogs. Listed symptoms include vomiting, lethargy, kidney failure and death.

ing_lupine.whatItIs: A legume seed, described in our data as a high protein legume.
ing_lupine.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein source.
ing_lupine.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts lupine's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_macadamia_nuts.whatItIs: A rich, oily tree nut used in confectionery and baking.
ing_macadamia_nuts.whyItsHere: Present as a nut ingredient in the product.
ing_macadamia_nuts.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for dogs, flagged as a critical safety concern: symptoms usually appear within twelve hours. Listed symptoms include weakness, incoordination, depression, vomiting, tremors and hyperthermia. Note: They are not known to be toxic to cats.

ing_mackerel_meal.whatItIs: Mackerel rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_mackerel_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated fish protein source.
ing_mackerel_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_magnesium_oxide.whatItIs: A mineral magnesium salt used as a supplement.
ing_magnesium_oxide.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its magnesium requirement.

ing_manganese_sulfate.whatItIs: A synthesised manganese salt, the common inorganic manganese supplement.
ing_manganese_sulfate.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts, associated in our data with bone and cartilage health.

ing_mannanoligosaccharides.whatItIs: Sugars from yeast cell walls. Note: They bind pathogens.
ing_mannanoligosaccharides.whyItsHere: Included as a prebiotic, associated in our data with immune support.

ing_mct_oil.whatItIs: Medium-chain triglycerides, a fat absorbed more directly than most. Note: It is easily digestible.
ing_mct_oil.whyItsHere: Included as a quickly available energy source.

ing_mealworm_protein.whatItIs: Protein from farmed mealworms. Note: It is sustainable and high in protein.
ing_mealworm_protein.whyItsHere: Included as an alternative protein source with a lower environmental cost.

ing_milk_protein.whatItIs: The combined casein and whey proteins from milk, extracted and dried.
ing_milk_protein.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source in the recipe.
ing_milk_protein.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts milk protein's allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy ingredient.

ing_molybdenum.whatItIs: A trace mineral. Note: It is essential in small amounts and acts as an enzyme cofactor.
ing_molybdenum.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts as a supplementary mineral.

ing_mung_beans.whatItIs: A small green pulse. Our data describes it as an easily digestible legume.
ing_mung_beans.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.

ing_oatmeal.whatItIs: Rolled or cut oats. Our data associates them with digestive health.
ing_oatmeal.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and for soluble fibre.

ing_onion.whatItIs: A bulb vegetable. Note: It contains N-propyl disulfide, which damages red blood cells.
ing_onion.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats and caution for dogs, flagged as a critical safety concern: all forms — raw, cooked and powder — are toxic and cause hemolytic anemia. Listed symptoms include gastrointestinal irritation, anemia, weakness, pale gums and elevated heart rate.

ing_pancreatin.whatItIs: A blend of digestive enzymes extracted from pancreas. Note: It contains protease, amylase and lipase.
ing_pancreatin.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive enzyme blend.

ing_panthenol.whatItIs: Pro-vitamin B5, which converts to pantothenic acid.
ing_panthenol.whyItsHere: Included as a supplementary nutrient, commonly in topical products.

ing_pantothenic_acid.whatItIs: Vitamin B5, supplied as d-Calcium pantothenate — the usual added form.
ing_pantothenic_acid.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in energy metabolism and hormone synthesis.

ing_pea_flour.whatItIs: Ground dried peas, contributing both protein and carbohydrate.
ing_pea_flour.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and carbohydrate source.

ing_peaches.whatItIs: A stone fruit with fuzzy skin, used without the pit. It contributes vitamins and fibre.
ing_peaches.whyItsHere: Included as a source of vitamins and fibre.
ing_peaches.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to remove the pit, noting it contains cyanide.

ing_peanut_hulls.whatItIs: The shell of the peanut, a by-product. Our data describes it as a low nutritional value fibre source.
ing_peanut_hulls.whyItsHere: Included as an insoluble fibre filler adding bulk.
ing_peanut_hulls.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium and describes it as low in nutritional value.

ing_pears.whatItIs: Pear fruit, contributing fibre and vitamins. A separate database entry from the singular 'Pear'.
ing_pears.whyItsHere: Included as a source of fibre and vitamins.
ing_pears.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to remove the seeds and core.

ing_pectinase.whatItIs: An enzyme that breaks down pectin, the soluble fibre in fruit.
ing_pectinase.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive enzyme helping break down fruit fibre.

ing_pediococcus_acidilactici.whatItIs: A lactic-acid bacterium from a different genus to the lactobacilli, cultured and dried.
ing_pediococcus_acidilactici.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic supporting digestion.

ing_pennyroyal.whatItIs: An essential oil from a mint-family plant. Note: It was historically used in flea products.
ing_pennyroyal.whyItsHere: Present as an essential oil in the product.
ing_pennyroyal.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: it is extremely toxic and causes liver failure. Its allergen risk is high.

ing_peppermint.whatItIs: A mint used dried or extracted. Our data restricts it to dogs, noting it can irritate cats. Our data lists it for dog products.
ing_peppermint.whyItsHere: Included for breath freshening and flavour.
ing_peppermint.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and notes it can be irritating to cats.

ing_permethrin.whatItIs: A synthesised insecticide used in flea products.
ing_permethrin.whyItsHere: Included as an insecticide in flea and tick treatments.
ing_permethrin.whatToWatchFor: Our data notes permethrin is extremely toxic to cats, and that cats can be poisoned by direct application or by close contact with a treated dog. It is rated caution and its allergen risk is medium.

ing_persimmon.whatItIs: A sweet orange fruit. Note: The flesh is generally safe in small amounts.
ing_persimmon.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution: the seeds and pits can cause intestinal obstruction or inflammation and are the main hazard. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea and intestinal obstruction.

ing_phytase.whatItIs: An enzyme that releases phosphorus locked up in plant phytate. Note: It improves mineral absorption from plant ingredients.
ing_phytase.whyItsHere: Included to make more of the plant-bound phosphorus available.

ing_pine_oil.whatItIs: An essential oil distilled from pine wood or needles.
ing_pine_oil.whyItsHere: Present as an essential oil in the product.
ing_pine_oil.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats and caution for dogs, flagged as a critical safety concern: it causes gastrointestinal upset and CNS depression and can damage the kidneys and liver. Its allergen risk is high.

ing_polysorbate_80.whatItIs: A synthesised emulsifier. Note: Its FDA GRAS status and common use in wet foods.
ing_polysorbate_80.whyItsHere: Added to keep fats and water mixed rather than separating.

ing_pork_fresh.whatItIs: Fresh meat from pigs, used as the main protein in the recipe.
ing_pork_fresh.whyItsHere: Included as the primary protein source for the diet.
ing_pork_fresh.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts pork's allergen risk at medium.

ing_pork_liver.whatItIs: Liver from pigs, an organ meat dense in micronutrients.
ing_pork_liver.whyItsHere: Included as a nutrient-dense organ meat.
ing_pork_liver.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts pork liver's allergen risk at medium.

ing_l_proline.whatItIs: An amino acid added in synthesised form. Note: Its importance for connective tissue.
ing_l_proline.whyItsHere: Added as a supplementary amino acid, involved in collagen synthesis.

ing_lactase.whatItIs: The enzyme that splits lactose. Note: It helps digest dairy products.
ing_lactase.whyItsHere: Included to help break down the lactose in dairy ingredients.

ing_lactobacillus_fermentum.whatItIs: A lactobacillus species originally isolated from fermented plant material.
ing_lactobacillus_fermentum.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic supporting digestion.

ing_lactobacillus_plantarum.whatItIs: A hardy lactobacillus species found in fermented vegetables, cultured and dried.
ing_lactobacillus_plantarum.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic supporting digestive health.

ing_pork_meal.whatItIs: Pork rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_pork_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_pork_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_potassium_chloride.whatItIs: A mineral salt used to supply potassium.
ing_potassium_chloride.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its potassium requirement.

ing_potassium_iodide.whatItIs: A synthesised potassium salt of iodine, a highly soluble way to supply the mineral.
ing_potassium_iodide.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts so the diet meets its iodine requirement.

ing_potato_flour.whatItIs: Dehydrated potato, ground into a fine flour.
ing_potato_flour.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source and as a binder.

ing_poultry_by_product_meal.whatItIs: Rendered and ground poultry by-products — the clean non-meat parts rather than breast meat.
ing_poultry_by_product_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_poultry_by_product_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium. Neither the bird nor the parts are named on the label.

ing_propyl_gallate.whatItIs: A synthetic antioxidant preservative. Note: It is often used alongside BHA and BHT.
ing_propyl_gallate.whyItsHere: Added to stop fats going rancid, extending shelf life.
ing_propyl_gallate.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution and notes it may cause stomach irritation in sensitive animals.

ing_protease.whatItIs: An enzyme that breaks protein into smaller pieces. Note: It aids protein digestion.
ing_protease.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive enzyme helping break down protein.

ing_pyridoxine_hydrochloride.whatItIs: The usual added form of vitamin B6 in a vitamin premix.
ing_pyridoxine_hydrochloride.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in protein metabolism and nerve function.

ing_rabbit_meal.whatItIs: Rabbit rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_rabbit_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated novel-protein source.

ing_raisins.whatItIs: Dried grapes. Note: Drying concentrates the risk further.
ing_raisins.whyItsHere: Present as a dried fruit in the product.
ing_raisins.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for dogs and caution for cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: they are more toxic per gram than fresh grapes and can cause acute kidney failure. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy, anorexia, abdominal pain and kidney failure.

ing_raw_yeast_dough.whatItIs: Unbaked bread dough containing live yeast. Note: It expands in the warm stomach and produces ethanol.
ing_raw_yeast_dough.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats: it can cause bloating, a twisted stomach and alcohol poisoning. Listed symptoms include bloated stomach, attempts to vomit, depression, disorientation, weakness, coma, seizures and hypothermia.

ing_red_lentils.whatItIs: A quick-cooking pulse contributing plant protein and fibre.
ing_red_lentils.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.

ing_rhubarb.whatItIs: A stalk vegetable. Note: The leaves contain high levels of oxalic acid.
ing_rhubarb.whyItsHere: Present as a vegetable or fruit ingredient.
ing_rhubarb.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats and caution for dogs: the leaves are toxic, and stalks are safer but can still cause gastrointestinal upset. Listed symptoms include drooling, vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy, weakness, tremors and kidney failure.

ing_riboflavin.whatItIs: Vitamin B2, supplied in its usual added form.
ing_riboflavin.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in energy metabolism.

ing_riboflavin_color.whatItIs: Vitamin B2 used for its colour rather than as a nutrient.
ing_riboflavin_color.whyItsHere: Added for yellow colour, using a vitamin rather than a synthetic dye.

ing_rosemary.whatItIs: The dried herb. Note: It is often used as a natural preservative.
ing_rosemary.whyItsHere: Added as a natural preservative and antioxidant.

ing_rye_flour.whatItIs: Ground rye grain. Our data notes it contains gluten.
ing_rye_flour.whatToWatchFor: Note: Rye flour contains gluten and puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_saccharomyces_boulardii.whatItIs: A probiotic yeast. Note: It is effective against antibiotic-associated diarrhoea.
ing_saccharomyces_boulardii.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic supporting digestion.

ing_saccharomyces_cerevisiae.whatItIs: Baker's or brewer's yeast, cultured and dried. It carries B vitamins.
ing_saccharomyces_cerevisiae.whyItsHere: Included as a probiotic yeast that also supplies B vitamins.

ing_salmon_fresh.whatItIs: Fresh salmon, an oily fish naturally rich in omega-3.
ing_salmon_fresh.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and as an omega-3 source.
ing_salmon_fresh.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts salmon's allergen risk at low for dogs but high for cats.

ing_salmon_meal.whatItIs: Salmon rendered and dried into a concentrated protein that also supplies omega-3.
ing_salmon_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein and omega-3 source.
ing_salmon_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low for dogs but high for cats.

ing_sardine.whatItIs: A small oily fish. Note: Small fish carry a lower mercury risk.
ing_sardine.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and as an omega-3 source.
ing_sardine.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts sardine's allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_sardine_meal.whatItIs: Sardines rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_sardine_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated fish protein source.
ing_sardine_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_sardine_oil.whatItIs: Oil extracted and refined from sardines, rich in omega-3.

ing_shallots.whatItIs: A bulb vegetable in the allium family, the same group as onion and garlic.
ing_shallots.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for cats and caution for dogs. The safety guidance says they contain the same toxic compounds as onions and can damage red blood cells. Listed symptoms include gastrointestinal irritation, anemia, weakness and pale gums.

ing_silver_vine.whatItIs: A dried plant. Our data describes it as an alternative to catnip that affects more cats. Our data lists it for cat products.
ing_silver_vine.whyItsHere: Included as an attractant for enrichment rather than nutrition.

ing_sodium_bisulfite.whatItIs: A synthesised sulfite used as a preservative.
ing_sodium_bisulfite.whyItsHere: Added as a preservative and antimicrobial.
ing_sodium_bisulfite.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution. It is a sulfite that can cause reactions in sensitive animals, and the allergen risk is medium.

ing_sodium_lauryl_sulfate.whatItIs: A synthesised surfactant used in shampoos.
ing_sodium_lauryl_sulfate.whyItsHere: Included in topical products as the cleansing agent.
ing_sodium_lauryl_sulfate.whatToWatchFor: Rated as caution. It can strip oils and irritate, and the allergen risk is medium.

ing_sodium_selenite.whatItIs: The inorganic form of selenium, described as such in our data.
ing_sodium_selenite.whyItsHere: Added in trace amounts so the diet meets its selenium requirement.

ing_soy_hulls.whatItIs: The outer coating of the soybean, separated during processing.
ing_soy_hulls.whyItsHere: Included as a fibre source adding bulk.

ing_soy_lecithin.whatItIs: An emulsifier extracted from soybeans that also supplies choline.
ing_soy_lecithin.whyItsHere: Added to keep fats and water mixed; it also contributes choline.
ing_soy_lecithin.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts soy lecithin's allergen risk at medium. It is soy-derived.

ing_soybeans.whatItIs: Whole soybeans. Note: They are a common allergen but have a complete amino acid profile.
ing_soybeans.whyItsHere: Included as a complete plant protein source.
ing_soybeans.whatToWatchFor: Our data describes soybeans as a common allergen and puts their allergen risk at medium.

ing_split_peas.whatItIs: Dried peas that have been split, contributing protein and fibre.
ing_split_peas.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.

ing_star_fruit.whatItIs: A tropical fruit. Note: It contains soluble calcium oxalate crystals.
ing_star_fruit.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, noting the oxalate crystals can cause acute kidney failure. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, weakness and kidney failure.

ing_sultanas.whatItIs: Dried grapes. Note: They carry the same kidney toxicity risk as raisins.
ing_sultanas.whyItsHere: Present as a dried fruit in the product.
ing_sultanas.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for dogs and caution for cats. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy, anorexia and kidney failure.

ing_sweet_potato.whatItIs: A starchy root vegetable. Our data describes it as a popular grain-free carbohydrate source.
ing_sweet_potato.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source that also supplies fibre and beta carotene.

ing_tamarind.whatItIs: A tangy pod fruit. Note: It contains tartaric acid, the same mechanism as grape toxicity.
ing_tamarind.whyItsHere: Present as a flavouring or fruit ingredient.
ing_tamarind.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for dogs and caution for cats, noting the tartaric acid can cause kidney toxicity by the same mechanism as grapes and raisins. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy, anorexia and kidney failure.

ing_tara_gum.whatItIs: A thickener extracted from tara tree seeds.
ing_tara_gum.whyItsHere: Added to thicken the food and hold its texture.

ing_tbhq.whatItIs: Tertiary butylhydroquinone, a synthetic antioxidant preservative.
ing_tbhq.whyItsHere: Added to stop fats going rancid, extending shelf life.
ing_tbhq.whatToWatchFor: Our data and the safety guidance both describe TBHQ as controversial: the FDA allows limited use, but some studies raise concerns about long-term exposure. It is rated caution.

ing_theobromine.whatItIs: The stimulant compound found in chocolate and cocoa.
ing_theobromine.whyItsHere: Present as a compound carried in by cocoa or chocolate.
ing_theobromine.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: even small amounts can cause vomiting, diarrhea, rapid breathing and seizures.

ing_thiamine_mononitrate.whatItIs: The usual added form of vitamin B1. Note: It is essential for cats and that deficiency is serious.
ing_thiamine_mononitrate.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in energy metabolism and nerve function.

ing_tocopherol.whatItIs: A single form of vitamin E, extracted rather than synthesised.
ing_tocopherol.whyItsHere: Added as a natural preservative; it is also a vitamin E source.

ing_tofu.whatItIs: Coagulated soy milk, pressed into a curd.
ing_tofu.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein source.
ing_tofu.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts tofu's allergen risk at medium. It is soy.

ing_trichoderma_longibrachiatum.whatItIs: A fermentation extract. Note: It is a source of cellulase enzyme.
ing_trichoderma_longibrachiatum.whyItsHere: Included as an enzyme source aiding fibre digestion.

ing_trout_meal.whatItIs: Trout rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_trout_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated fish protein source.
ing_trout_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_tuna_fresh.whatItIs: Fresh tuna, an oily marine fish that cats find unusually appealing.
ing_tuna_fresh.whyItsHere: Included for its protein and because animals find it very palatable.
ing_tuna_fresh.whatToWatchFor: Rated safe in moderation and says to limit exposure because of mercury concerns. Its allergen risk is low for dogs but high for cats.

ing_turkey_fat.whatItIs: Fat rendered from turkey, an energy-dense ingredient that carries flavour.
ing_turkey_fat.whyItsHere: Included as an energy source and to make the food more appealing.
ing_turkey_fat.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium.

ing_turkey_fresh.whatItIs: Fresh poultry meat from turkey, used as the main protein.
ing_turkey_fresh.whyItsHere: Included as the primary protein source for the diet.
ing_turkey_fresh.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts turkey's allergen risk at medium.

ing_turkey_meal.whatItIs: Turkey rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_turkey_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_turkey_meal.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium.

ing_turmeric_color.whatItIs: Ground turmeric used for its colour. Note: The yellow comes from curcumin.
ing_turmeric_color.whyItsHere: Added for yellow colour, using a spice rather than a synthetic dye.

ing_vegetable_glycerin.whatItIs: Glycerin extracted from vegetable oils, which holds on to water.
ing_vegetable_glycerin.whyItsHere: Added to retain moisture, keeping softer products from drying out.

ing_venison_meal.whatItIs: Venison rendered and dried into a concentrated protein.
ing_venison_meal.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated novel-protein source.

ing_vitamin_a_supplement.whatItIs: A synthesised form of vitamin A. Note: It is fat-soluble.
ing_vitamin_a_supplement.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in vision, immune function and skin health.
ing_vitamin_a_supplement.whatToWatchFor: Note: Vitamin A is fat-soluble and that excess can be toxic, so it accumulates rather than being flushed out.

ing_vitamin_k1.whatItIs: Phytonadione, the natural form of vitamin K. Our data describes it as safer than menadione, the synthetic K3 form.
ing_vitamin_k1.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, involved in blood clotting and bone metabolism.

ing_vitamin_k_supplement.whatItIs: A vitamin K supplement, recorded as supplied in the menadione form.
ing_vitamin_k_supplement.whyItsHere: Included as a required nutrient, essential for blood coagulation.

ing_watermelon.whatItIs: A melon that is mostly water, contributing hydration and vitamins.
ing_watermelon.whyItsHere: Included for its moisture and vitamins.
ing_watermelon.whatToWatchFor: Our data says to remove the seeds and rind.

ing_whey_protein_concentrate.whatItIs: Whey filtered and concentrated. Note: It has a higher protein content than regular whey.
ing_whey_protein_concentrate.whyItsHere: Included as a concentrated protein source.
ing_whey_protein_concentrate.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at medium. It is a dairy-derived ingredient.

ing_white_beans.whatItIs: A mild white bean contributing plant protein and fibre.
ing_white_beans.whyItsHere: Included as a plant protein and fibre source.

ing_whitefish_fresh.whatItIs: A general term for mild white-fleshed fish. The species is not named.
ing_whitefish_fresh.whyItsHere: Included as a protein source in the recipe.
ing_whitefish_fresh.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts its allergen risk at low to medium, and the species is not identified on the label.

ing_whole_egg.whatItIs: The complete egg. Our data describes it as a highly digestible protein source.
ing_whole_egg.whyItsHere: Included as a complete protein and as a binder.
ing_whole_egg.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts whole egg's allergen risk at medium.

ing_whole_wheat.whatItIs: Wheat with all three parts of the grain intact. Note: It contains bran, germ and endosperm.
ing_whole_wheat.whyItsHere: Included as a carbohydrate source that also supplies fibre.
ing_whole_wheat.whatToWatchFor: Our data puts whole wheat's allergen risk at medium.

ing_wintergreen_oil.whatItIs: An essential oil. Note: It contains methyl salicylate, an aspirin-like compound.
ing_wintergreen_oil.whyItsHere: Present as an essential oil in the product.
ing_wintergreen_oil.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, flagged as a critical safety concern, singling out cats. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea and aspirin-like toxicity. Its allergen risk is high.

ing_xylanase.whatItIs: An enzyme that breaks down hemicellulose in plant cell walls.
ing_xylanase.whyItsHere: Included as a digestive enzyme helping break down plant fibre.

ing_xylitol.whatItIs: A sugar alcohol used as a sweetener. Our data describes ingestion as a medical emergency.
ing_xylitol.whyItsHere: Present as a sweetener in the product.
ing_xylitol.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for dogs, flagged as a critical safety concern: it causes dangerously low blood sugar and liver injury, and should be treated as an emergency exposure. Listed symptoms include vomiting, weakness, incoordination, seizures, liver failure and hypoglycemia.

ing_yeast_dough.whatItIs: Unbaked bread dough containing live, active yeast.
ing_yeast_dough.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for both dogs and cats, flagged as a critical safety concern: raw dough expands in the warm stomach causing bloat and produces alcohol as it ferments — the safety guidance calls this a double threat.

ing_zante_currants.whatItIs: Small dried fruit. Note: These are actually dried grapes rather than true currants.
ing_zante_currants.whyItsHere: Present as a dried fruit in the product.
ing_zante_currants.whatToWatchFor: Rated toxic for dogs and caution for cats, noting they carry the same risk as raisins. Listed symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy, anorexia and kidney failure.

ing_zinc_methionine.whatItIs: Zinc bound to the amino acid methionine. Our data describes it as a highly bioavailable zinc form.
ing_zinc_methionine.whyItsHere: Added as a more absorbable zinc source.

ing_zinc_sulfate.whatItIs: A synthesised zinc salt, the common inorganic zinc supplement.
ing_zinc_sulfate.whyItsHere: Added so the diet meets its zinc requirement, associated with skin and immune health.
